quick: The risen Lord is real: “Touch me and see.”
“Go and make disciples of all nations”: every baptised person is sent.
“I am with you always, to the end of the age.”
2027-04-25.action: Speak one word of faith or hope to a colleague or neighbour this week.
2027-04-25.question: Where is the Lord sending me as his witness this week?
2027-04-25.special: Fourth Sunday after Qyomtho. Feast of St Mark. (In 2025–26 also Laity Day; check the collection.)
illus: An illustration

A Kerala teacher in a government school never preached, but her honesty, patience and care for poor students made colleagues ask: “Why are you like this?” She answered simply: “Because of Jesus.” That is lay apostolate.

family.explain: Before going back to the Father, Jesus told his friends: “Go and tell everyone about me. I am with you always.” He says this to us too!
family.intention: We pray for missionaries and for courage to tell others about Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “How can our family show Jesus' love to our neighbours?”

catechism: The vocation of the lay faithful.
kidsaint: A Jesuit missionary who came to India and travelled along the coasts, baptising thousands and teaching children their prayers. He went as far as Japan. Lesson: Jesus sends each of us to share his love.
term: In the 2025–26 lectionary the Fourth Sunday after Qyomtho is Syro-Malankara Catholic Laity Day, when the Church prays for the lay faithful and supports their works.
termMore: Christ's last command in Matthew (28:18–20): go, make disciples, baptise, teach. It is the charter of the Church's mission.

quick: The Sadducees' question was a trap; Jesus answered that they knew neither the Scriptures nor the power of God.
God is the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob: the God of the living.
Psalm 8 is fulfilled in Jesus, crowned with glory because he tasted death for everyone.
2027-04-01.action: Pray by name for three of your departed, with the words “alive to you, Lord.”
2027-04-01.question: Do I believe, deep down, that those I have lost are alive to God?

family.explain: Some people asked Jesus a tricky question because they did not believe that the dead will rise. Jesus answered that God told Moses, “I am the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob,” long after those men had died. That means they are alive to God. Jesus himself rose from the dead at Easter, and he promises that we too will live with him.
family.intention: We pray for our grandparents and all in our family who have died, that they may live with God in joy.
family.ask: Ask: “Whom in our family do we want to see again in heaven?”

illus: An illustration

A schoolteacher in Pala lost her husband in the week before Lent. On Easter night she stood in church with her two sons, and when the people answered “He is risen indeed,” she could not say the words. On the Thursday of Hevoro week her younger son, who was nine, asked her why the priest had read about Abraham being alive. She told him what she had heard: that God calls himself the God of Abraham, so Abraham must be living. The boy thought for a moment and said, “Then God is also Appachan's God.” That evening, for the first time since the funeral, she lit the lamp and said the Easter greeting aloud.

pm.open: Christ is risen! Lord Jesus, God of the living, we gather in your Easter light. Open our hearts to the power of God. Amen.
share: Is not this the reason you are wrong, that you know neither the scriptures nor the power of God? (Mark 12:24). Where do I limit what God can do?
He is God not of the dead, but of the living (Mark 12:27). How does this change the way I grieve?
But we do see Jesus… crowned with glory and honor (Hebrews 2:9). What do I see when I look at Jesus today?
pm.resp: Risen Lord, you are the God of the living.
interc: For the Church in this Easter week, that she may proclaim the resurrection of the body with joy and courage.
For all who mourn this Easter, especially those who lost someone during Lent.
For married couples, that their love may be faithful and holy.
For those who mock or doubt the faith, that they may come to know the power of God.
For all our departed, that they may rejoice in the light of the risen Christ.
pm.close: Father, you are the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, and in your sight no one who belongs to you is lost. Strengthen our faith in the resurrection, comfort those who grieve, and bring us with all our departed to the glory your Son has entered. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: This Friday after the Resurrection the Church remembers all the confessors, who confessed Christ at the cost of suffering or death.
Hebrews calls the heroes of faith people “of whom the world was not worthy.”
Jesus promises to acknowledge before the Father everyone who acknowledges him before others.
2027-04-02.action: Pray by name for one community where Christians are persecuted today.
2027-04-02.question: Where does fear keep me silent about Christ?

family.explain: Jesus told his friends not to be afraid. God takes care of even a little sparrow, and he knows how many hairs are on our heads. Many Christians, long ago and today, have been brave and said “I belong to Jesus,” even when people were cruel to them. Today the Church remembers all of them. Jesus says that when we speak up for him, he will speak up for us before his Father.
family.intention: We pray for Christians who are being hurt or treated badly because they love Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “Where can each of us be brave for Jesus this week?”

illus: An illustration

A young engineer from Kollam joined a firm abroad where his team leader liked to make jokes about religion at lunch. For months he laughed along and said nothing. In Hevoro week he read, in a small book of saints his mother had packed, about the Christians of the early centuries who were offered release if they would only say one word against Christ. The next day, when the jokes began, he said quietly, “I am a Christian, and I would rather you did not laugh at the things I love.” There was a silence. Later, a colleague from another country stopped him in the corridor and said that she was a Catholic too, and had never dared to say so.

pm.open: Christ is risen! Lord Jesus, on this Friday of All the Confessors we thank you for all who acknowledged you before others. Give us their courage. Amen.
share: Of whom the world was not worthy (Hebrews 11:38). Which witness of the faith has touched my life most?
So do not be afraid; you are of more value than many sparrows (Matthew 10:31). What fear do I bring to the Lord tonight?
Everyone therefore who acknowledges me before others, I also will acknowledge before my Father in heaven (Matthew 10:32). Where is the Lord asking me to acknowledge him?
pm.resp: Risen Lord, make us faithful confessors of your name.
interc: For the Church in every land where Christians are persecuted, that they may be strong and that their persecutors may come to know Christ.
For Christians in India who suffer for their faith, and for peace and justice in our country.
For those who are tempted to deny the faith out of fear, that the Lord may hold them fast.
For all who have died for Christ, that they may rejoice in the white robes of the Lamb.
For ourselves, that we may confess Christ with gentleness and courage in our homes and workplaces.
pm.close: Father, in every age you have raised up confessors who bore witness to your Son with their lives. Let their example and their prayers make us faithful, deliver us from fear, and bring us with them to the glory of the Resurrection. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Jesus is the apostle sent to us and the high priest who goes to the Father for us.
Moses was faithful as a servant in God's house; Christ is faithful over it as the Son, and we are his house.
Jesus told John not to stop someone casting out demons in his name: whoever is not against you is for you.
2027-04-03.action: Thank God today for one good thing done in Jesus' name by someone outside your own circle.
2027-04-03.question: Am I jealous of good that others do, or do I rejoice in it?

family.explain: John saw a man helping people in Jesus' name, but the man was not one of Jesus' twelve friends. John tried to stop him. Jesus said, “Do not stop him.” Jesus is happy when anyone does good in his name. We are all part of God's big family, his house.
family.intention: We pray for all Christians everywhere, that we may love one another and work together for Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “Who is someone doing good for Jesus whom we can thank or help this week?”

illus: An illustration

Two parish youth groups in a town near Kottayam, from two different Churches, used to arrange their Easter-week visits to the old-age home on the same afternoon, and each group quietly resented the other for crowding the place. One year the leader of one group rang the other and asked whether they would come together instead. They arrived on the Saturday of Easter week with one set of songs, one cake, and twice as many hands. An old man who had not spoken much since his wife died sang every Easter hymn with them. At the end the matron said it was the first time she had seen both groups laugh together.

pm.open: Christ is risen! Lord Jesus, apostle and high priest, we are your house. Build us up in faith and hope as we close this white week. Amen.
share: Consider that Jesus, the apostle and high priest of our confession, was faithful (Hebrews 3:1–2). What does it mean for me to consider Jesus today?
We are his house if we hold firm the confidence and the pride that belong to hope (Hebrews 3:6). Where has my hope weakened since Easter?
Do not stop him; for whoever is not against you is for you (Luke 9:50). Where am I tempted to be jealous of good done by others?
pm.resp: Risen Lord, build us into your house.
interc: For the whole Church, the house of God, that she may be holy and united.
For Christians of all Churches, that the Spirit may lead us to the unity Christ prayed for.
For those whose Easter joy has already faded, that the Lord may renew their hope.
For those preparing for confession today, that they may meet the mercy of the risen Lord.
For our parish as we prepare for New Sunday, that we may confess with Thomas, My Lord and my God.
pm.close: Father, your Son is faithful over your house as the Son, and we are his house. Keep us firm in hope, deliver us from jealousy, and gather all who do good in his name into the joy of his Resurrection. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Paul, in chains, writes: “Remember Jesus Christ, raised from the dead”; the word of God is not chained.
If we are faithless, the Lord remains faithful, for he cannot deny himself.
In the parable the beloved son is killed, but the stone that the builders rejected becomes the cornerstone.
2027-04-05.action: Say slowly before sleep tonight: “Remember Jesus Christ, raised from the dead.”
2027-04-05.question: Am I treating the vineyard God gave me as mine, or as his?

family.explain: Jesus told a story about a man who planted a vineyard and let some workers look after it. When he sent people to collect the grapes, the workers were cruel to them. At last he sent his own son, and they killed him. Jesus was telling about himself: he is God's beloved Son, and he would be killed. But he also said that the stone the builders threw away became the most important stone. That is Easter! God raised Jesus up.
family.intention: We pray that our family may look after everything God has given us, and give him thanks.
family.ask: Ask: “What has God given our family to look after?”

illus: An illustration

A retired bank clerk in Thrissur visits the district jail once a month with the prison ministry of his parish. One Easter Monday a young inmate, who had refused to speak at every earlier visit, asked him why he bothered to come. He answered that the apostle Paul had also been in prison and had written that the word of God is not chained. The young man said nothing. Two years later a letter came to the parish office from another town. The writer had been released, had found work in a bakery, and asked the old man to pray for his wedding. At the bottom he had copied one line: “The word of God is not chained.”

pm.open: Christ is risen! Lord Jesus, raised from the dead, we remember you and you are with us. Open our hearts to your word, which no chain can bind. Amen.
share: Remember Jesus Christ, raised from the dead (2 Timothy 2:8). How do I remember Jesus in my daily life?
If we are faithless, he remains faithful, for he cannot deny himself (2 Timothy 2:13). Where do I need to trust his faithfulness more than my own?
The stone that the builders rejected has become the cornerstone (Mark 12:10). Where have I felt rejected, and how might the Lord build on it?
pm.resp: Risen Lord, you remain faithful.
interc: For the Church, the Lord's vineyard, that her leaders and people may give God the fruit of faith and love.
For Christians imprisoned for their faith, and for all prisoners and their families.
For prison chaplains and all who visit those in jail.
For those who feel rejected or thrown aside, that they may find their place in Christ.
For all who have grown faithless, that they may return to the One who remains faithful.
pm.close: Father, you sent your beloved Son to the vineyard, and when he was rejected you raised him up as the cornerstone. Make us faithful stewards of all you have given us, release all who are bound, and keep us mindful of Jesus Christ, raised from the dead. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: “But God, who is rich in mercy… made us alive together with Christ”: Easter has begun in us through Baptism.
We are saved by grace through faith, and created in Christ Jesus for good works.
Jesus rebuked the fever; Simon's mother-in-law got up at once and served.
2027-04-06.action: Do one act of service today at once, without being asked.
2027-04-06.question: What fever is the Lord asking to rebuke in me?

family.explain: Jesus went to Peter's house. Peter's mother-in-law was sick with a high fever. Jesus stood near her and told the fever to go, and it went away! At once she got up and served them food. That evening many sick people came, and Jesus put his hands on each one and healed them. Jesus cares about every single person.
family.intention: We pray for everyone we know who is sick, that Jesus may touch and heal them.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we serve someone in our home today, as Peter's mother-in-law did?”

illus: An illustration

A grandmother in Changanassery had been bedridden for weeks with a fever that would not leave. On the Tuesday after New Sunday the parish priest brought her Holy Communion and read the Gospel of Simon's mother-in-law. She smiled and said, “When I get up, I will make you tea.” The fever broke two days later, slowly, as fevers do. On the next Sunday she was too weak to go to church, but when the priest came again she was sitting in the kitchen, and she made him tea with her own hands. “He got me up so that I could serve,” she said. “That is what the Gospel says.”

pm.open: Christ is risen! Lord Jesus, you made us alive together with you. Come into our gathering as you came into Simon's house, and raise us up to serve. Amen.
share: But God, who is rich in mercy… made us alive together with Christ (Ephesians 2:4–5). Where have I seen God's mercy bring me back to life?
We are what he has made us, created in Christ Jesus for good works (Ephesians 2:10). What good work is the Lord preparing for me now?
Immediately she got up and began to serve them (Luke 4:39). How does the Lord want me to serve after he has healed me?
pm.resp: Risen Lord, raise us up to serve you.
interc: For the newly baptized of this Easter, that they may live as people made alive in Christ.
For all who are sick, especially those we name in our hearts, that the Lord may lay his hands on each of them.
For doctors, nurses and caregivers, that they may serve with skill and love.
For those trapped in the fever of sin or addiction, that the Lord may rebuke it and release them.
For our families, that we may serve one another readily and joyfully.
pm.close: Father, rich in mercy, you made us alive with your Son when we were dead through our sins. Heal the sick, raise up the weak, and make us walk in the good works you have prepared for us. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: In Christ, those who were far off have been brought near by his blood, into the hope of Israel's covenants.
He is our peace: he broke down the dividing wall of hostility, and through him all have access in one Spirit to the Father.
A lamp is put on a lampstand; pay attention to how you listen.
2027-04-07.action: Take one step this week toward someone you have kept at a distance.
2027-04-07.question: Which wall in my life am I still rebuilding?

family.explain: St Paul says that Jesus is our peace. Long ago there was a wall between groups of people who would not be friends. Jesus broke down that wall by dying on the cross and rising again, so that everyone can be one family in God. Sometimes we build walls too, when we stay angry or refuse to talk to someone. Jesus wants to help us break them down.
family.intention: We pray for families and neighbors who are not speaking to each other, that Jesus may bring them peace.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there someone we need to make peace with this week?”

illus: An illustration

Two brothers in a village near Pathanamthitta had not spoken for eleven years over a strip of land between their houses. Their aged mother lived with the elder brother and went to church alone. In the week after New Sunday the younger brother's daughter, home from nursing college, heard the reading “he has broken down the dividing wall.” That evening she walked across the strip of land with a box of Easter cake and knocked on her uncle's door. Her uncle opened it, looked at her for a long time, and called his wife. The brothers did not settle the land that year. But on the next Sunday they stood together in church for the first time in eleven years, with their mother between them.

pm.open: Christ is risen! Lord Jesus, you are our peace. Break down every wall among us and open our ears to your word. Amen.
share: But now in Christ Jesus you who once were far off have been brought near by the blood of Christ (Ephesians 2:13). When did I feel far from God, and how did he bring me near?
He is our peace; in his flesh he has made both groups into one and has broken down the dividing wall (Ephesians 2:14). Which wall in my life does Christ want to break down?
Pay attention to how you listen (Luke 8:18). How do I listen to God's word, and to others?
pm.resp: Risen Lord, you are our peace.
interc: For the unity of all Christians, especially among the Churches of the St Thomas tradition.
For the Jewish people, the first to hear the word of God, and for friendship between Christians and Jews.
For families and neighbors divided by quarrels, that the risen Lord may bring them peace.
For communities wounded by caste and prejudice, that all may know they are one in Christ.
For ourselves, that we may listen to God's word with faith and let his light shine.
pm.close: Father, through your Son, who is our peace, you have brought near those who were far off and given all of us access to you in one Spirit. Break down the walls that divide us, make us people who listen with faith, and let the light of the Resurrection shine through our lives. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Hebrews asks us to remember our leaders, consider the end of their lives and imitate their faith.
The faithful servant feeds the household at the proper time and is found at work when the master comes.
We have an altar, the sacrifice of Christ, and from it we offer the sacrifice of praise and of sharing.
2027-04-08.action: Pray by name for one shepherd who brought you the faith.
2027-04-08.question: What has the Lord put in my charge, and will he find me at work when he comes?

family.explain: Jesus told a story about a servant whose master went away and left him in charge of the house. His job was to give everyone their food on time. When the master came back and found him doing his job well, he was very happy and gave him even more to look after. Jesus has given each of us something to look after: our family, our studies, our friends.
family.intention: We pray for our bishop and priests, and for the bishops who have died.
family.ask: Ask: “What has Jesus given me to look after at home?”

illus: An illustration

A retired headmaster in a parish near Pathanamthitta kept a small notebook with the names of everyone who had taught him the faith: his grandmother, the Sunday school teacher, the priest who prepared him for his First Holy Qurbono, the bishop who confirmed him. On the anniversary of each death he wrote a date beside the name and went to the Holy Qurbono for that person. His grandson once asked why he bothered, since most of the names were people nobody remembered. The old man said, “They fed me when I was hungry for God. Someone has to say thank you.” When he died, the grandson found the notebook and added one more name.

pm.open: Christ is risen! Lord Jesus, you are the same yesterday and today and forever. Be among us now as our Good Shepherd. Amen.
share: Remember your leaders, those who spoke the word of God to you (Hebrews 13:7). Whose faith do I want to imitate?
Blessed is that slave whom his master will find at work when he arrives (Matthew 24:46). What work has the Lord given me?
Do not neglect to do good and to share what you have (Hebrews 13:16). What can I share this week?
pm.resp: Good Shepherd, make us faithful stewards.
interc: For our bishops, priests and deacons, that they may feed the Lord's household faithfully.
For Most Rev. Lawrence Mar Ephrem and all the bishops of our Church who have died, that they may rest in the risen Lord.
For parents and teachers who hand on the faith to children.
For those who have lost hope in the Church because of an unfaithful steward.
For the poor with whom we can share what we have.
pm.close: Father, your Son is the same yesterday and today and forever. Bless the shepherds of your Church, give rest to those who have finished their course, and make each of us a faithful and wise servant until he comes. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Paul persecuted the Church until God, through grace, revealed his Son to him.
After his call he spent hidden years in Arabia and Damascus before visiting Cephas.
Jesus put a little child by his side: the least among you is the greatest.
2027-04-09.action: Pray today for someone you think will never change.
2027-04-09.question: When people see my life, do they glorify God?

family.explain: The disciples were arguing about who was the most important among them. Jesus brought a little child and made the child stand next to him. He said that whoever welcomes a little child in his name welcomes him. In God's family the one who is small and humble is the greatest.
family.intention: We pray for children who are not welcomed or loved.
family.ask: Ask: “How can I make someone feel welcome tomorrow?”

illus: An illustration

A young man in Kollam was known in his street for fighting and drinking. His mother went every Friday to the parish church and lit a candle for him. Neighbours told her she was wasting her money. One year, during Holy Week, he went to confession for the first time in eleven years, after a friend of his died in a road accident. He changed slowly, with many falls. Some years later he was leading the youth group's visits to the de-addiction centre. An old neighbour who had warned his mother stopped her outside the church and said, “I have seen it with my own eyes. Your God is great.”

pm.open: Christ is risen! Lord Jesus, you called Paul by your grace. Call us again today, and open our hearts to your word. Amen.
share: God called me through his grace (Galatians 1:15). Where has God's grace turned my life?
I went away at once into Arabia (Galatians 1:17). Do I give God hidden time to shape me?
The least among all of you is the greatest (Luke 9:48). Where do I still want to be the greatest?
pm.resp: Risen Lord, change our hearts.
interc: For those who persecute the Church today, that they may meet the risen Christ.
For people struggling with addiction, and for their families who wait and pray.
For new converts and the newly baptized of this Easter.
For children who are neglected or unwanted.
For humility among leaders in our parishes and communities.
pm.close: Father, you revealed your Son to Paul and made a persecutor into an apostle. Turn the hearts of all who are far from you, make us humble like little children, and let our lives give you glory. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: After fourteen years Paul laid his gospel before the leaders in Jerusalem, so as not to run in vain.
Titus was not compelled to be circumcised: we are saved by grace in Christ, and God shows no partiality.
Jesus grieves over towns that saw his works and did not repent; whoever listens to his messengers listens to him.
2027-04-10.action: Pick one word from Scripture this week and do it.
2027-04-10.question: What have I heard from God many times without changing?

family.explain: Jesus sent his friends to tell people about God. He said: if people listen to you, they are listening to me. Today Jesus still speaks to us through the Bible, through our priests and through our parents and teachers when they teach us about him. Listening is not only hearing with our ears; it is doing what we hear.
family.intention: We pray for our parish priest and for all who teach us the faith.
family.ask: Ask: “What did we hear in church last Sunday, and did we do it?”

illus: An illustration

A young engineer in Kottayam had a gift for leading Bible study, and his group grew fast. Some of his ideas were new, and a few people were uneasy. Instead of defending himself angrily, he took his notes to the parish priest and asked him to read them. The priest pointed out two places where his teaching had drifted from the faith of the Church. The young man changed them, and told his group openly what he had corrected. Several members said later that this, more than any talk he gave, made them trust him.

pm.open: Christ is risen! Lord Jesus, you said, “Whoever listens to you listens to me.” Open our ears and our hearts to your word this evening. Amen.
share: In order to make sure that I was not running, or had not run, in vain (Galatians 2:2). Do I test my ideas with the faith of the Church?
God shows no partiality (Galatians 2:6). Whom do I treat as less important?
If the deeds of power done in you had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago (Luke 10:13). What has God done for me that should have changed me?
pm.resp: Lord, give us listening hearts.
interc: For the Pope and the bishops in communion with him, that they may guard the truth of the Gospel.
For preachers and catechists, that they may speak the word faithfully.
For all who have heard the Gospel many times and grown cold.
For an end to partiality and division in our parishes.
For those preparing to receive the sacraments in this Easter season.
pm.close: Father, you sent your Son, and he sends us. Keep us in the communion of the apostles, deliver us from partiality, and make us people who hear your word and keep it, like the holy Virgin Mary. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Justified by faith, we have peace with God through Jesus Christ and stand in grace.
Suffering produces endurance, character and hope, because God's love is poured into our hearts.
St Julius welcomed St Athanasius; whoever welcomes Christ's messengers, even with a cup of cold water, welcomes Christ.
2027-04-12.action: Welcome one newcomer or stranger this week.
2027-04-12.question: Whom does the Lord want me to welcome in his name?
kidsaint: Julius was the Pope, the bishop of Rome, long ago. A brave bishop named Athanasius was chased out of his city for teaching that Jesus is truly God. Julius welcomed him to Rome, listened to him and stood up for him, even though powerful people were angry. Lesson: stand up for the truth, and be kind to someone others are treating badly.

family.explain: Jesus said that when we welcome his friends, we are welcoming him. Even giving a glass of cold water to someone in his name is something God never forgets. Long ago Pope Julius welcomed a bishop named Athanasius who had nowhere to go. We can welcome people too: a new child in class, a visitor at home, a lonely neighbour.
family.intention: We pray for the Pope and for families who have had to leave their homes.
family.ask: Ask: “Who is new or lonely around us, and how can we welcome them?”

illus: An illustration

A family in Thodupuzha noticed that the young men from Odisha who worked at the construction site near their house ate their lunch sitting on the road. One Sunday after the Holy Qurbono the mother sent her son out with a jug of cold water and a plate of banana fritters. The men were shy at first. Over the next months the family learned their names, and the youngest of them, far from his own mother, began to call her Amma. When the building was finished and the workers left, he came to the gate to say goodbye and could hardly speak. The son said later, “It started with a jug of water.”

pm.open: Christ is risen! Lord Jesus, you give us your peace. Welcome us into your presence now, and teach us to welcome others. Amen.
share: We have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ (Romans 5:1). Where do I still live as if God were against me?
Suffering produces endurance, and endurance produces character, and character produces hope (Romans 5:3–4). What has suffering produced in me?
Whoever gives even a cup of cold water to one of these little ones (Matthew 10:42). What small welcome can I give this week?
pm.resp: Lord, make us people of welcome.
interc: For Pope N. and all the bishops, that like St Julius they may guard the faith with courage.
For those who suffer for the truth of the faith.
For refugees, migrant workers and all who are far from home.
For the sick, that suffering may become hope for them.
For our parish, that every newcomer may find a home among us.
pm.close: Father, through your risen Son you have given us peace and poured your love into our hearts. By the prayers of St Julius, make us strong in the faith and generous in welcome, that in receiving the least we may receive Christ. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Jesus prayed with loud cries and tears and was heard: the Father's answer was the Resurrection.
Christ was appointed by the Father a high priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek.
The disciples asked, “Lord, teach us to pray,” and Jesus gave them the Our Father.
2027-04-13.action: Pray the Our Father once today, slowly.
2027-04-13.question: When I pray, do I speak to God as my Father?

family.explain: The disciples watched Jesus praying, and they wanted to pray like him. So they asked, “Lord, teach us to pray.” Jesus taught them the prayer we call the Our Father. It begins by calling God Father, because through Jesus we are God's children. We say this prayer in the Holy Qurbono, just before Holy Communion.
family.intention: We pray for everyone who finds it hard to pray.
family.ask: Ask: “Which line of the Our Father do you like best, and why?”

illus: An illustration

A grandmother in Mavelikara had prayed for many years for her son, who had left the Church after a bitter quarrel with a priest. She prayed the Our Father every evening and stopped each time at the words about forgiving. One evening she realized that she had never forgiven the priest either. She wrote him a short letter and posted it before she could change her mind. Some months later her son came home for her birthday. He did not come back to the Church at once, but at the evening prayer he stood beside her, and when she began the Our Father, he joined in.

pm.open: Christ is risen! Lord Jesus, you taught your disciples to pray. Teach us now, as we gather in your name. Amen.
share: He offered up prayers and supplications, with loud cries and tears (Hebrews 5:7). Do I bring my tears to God?
He learned obedience through what he suffered (Hebrews 5:8). What has suffering taught me?
Lord, teach us to pray (Luke 11:1). What would I like the Lord to teach me about prayer?
pm.resp: Father, hallowed be your name.
interc: For the Church, that her prayer may be united with the prayer of Christ the High Priest.
For our priests, who stand at the altar in the person of Christ.
For those who pray with tears and feel unheard.
For those who find it hard to forgive.
For families who no longer pray together.
pm.close: Father, you heard the cries of your Son and raised him in glory. Hear the prayers of your children, forgive us as we forgive, and keep us in the time of trial. Through Christ our Lord, our High Priest forever. Amen.

quick: Hebrews calls us to go on toward perfection: the foundation of faith is laid in order to build.
Mar Shemun Bar Sabbae, bishop of Seleucia-Ctesiphon, refused to betray his flock and died a martyr in Persia in the fourth century.
Jesus teaches persistent prayer: ask, search, knock; the Father gives the Holy Spirit to those who ask.
2027-04-14.action: Begin praying daily for the Holy Spirit until Pentecost.
2027-04-14.question: What do I keep asking God for, and do I ask for the Holy Spirit?
kidsaint: Mar Shemun was a bishop in Persia, a land far to the east, about 1,700 years ago. The king told him to make the poor Christians pay a huge tax and to worship the sun. Shemun said no: he loved his people, and he would worship only God, who made the sun. He died for Jesus on a Good Friday. Lesson: love the people God gives you, and never be ashamed to belong to Jesus.

family.explain: Jesus told us to keep asking God, like a friend who knocks on a door at midnight until it opens. He said that if parents know how to give good things to their children, God our Father will give even more: he will give us the Holy Spirit. The Holy Spirit makes us brave and loving. Long ago in Persia, Bishop Mar Shemun was so brave that he gave his life for Jesus.
family.intention: We pray for Christians who are persecuted for their faith today.
family.ask: Ask: “What shall we ask God for together every day this week?”

illus: An illustration

A small prayer group in a parish near Adoor met every Wednesday evening. For three years they prayed for a young couple in the parish who had no children and for a man in the group whose brother had left the faith and would not speak to the family. Some members gave up and stopped coming. The others kept going, though nothing seemed to change. In the fourth year the couple's daughter was born. The brother did not return, but when the man fell ill, the brother came to the hospital and sat with him every night. “We did not get everything we asked for,” the group leader said, “but God answered more than we knew how to ask.”

pm.open: Christ is risen! Heavenly Father, your Son told us to ask, search and knock. We come knocking now: give us your Holy Spirit. Amen.
share: Let us go on toward perfection (Hebrews 6:1). Where have I stopped growing in faith?
Ground that drinks up the rain... receives a blessing from God (Hebrews 6:7). What fruit has Easter produced in me?
At least because of his persistence he will get up and give him whatever he needs (Luke 11:8). For what have I given up praying?
pm.resp: Heavenly Father, give us your Holy Spirit.
interc: For Christians persecuted for their faith, especially in the lands of the East where Mar Shemun gave his life.
For those who have fallen away from the faith, that they may come back like Usthazanes.
For the newly baptized, that they may grow toward perfection.
For couples longing for children, and for all whose prayers seem unanswered.
For a new outpouring of the Holy Spirit on our Church as we walk toward Pentecost.
pm.close: Father, you give good gifts to your children and the Holy Spirit to those who ask. By the prayers of Mar Shemun Bar Sabbae and all the martyrs, strengthen the persecuted, bring back the lost, and let us bear fruit for your glory. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Jesus is priest not by descent but through the power of an indestructible life: his priesthood rests on his Resurrection.
Being near the Lord is not enough; we must strive to enter through the narrow door.
People will come from east and west to eat in the kingdom of God, and we are among them.
2027-04-15.action: Pray today for one priest by name.
2027-04-15.question: Am I content to stand near Jesus, or am I striving to enter through the door?

family.explain: Someone asked Jesus how many people would be saved. Jesus did not give a number. He said: try hard to go in through the narrow door. A narrow door is one we pass through by bending low and leaving our big bags of pride outside. Jesus also said that people from every side of the world will come and sit at God's great feast. Our family is invited too.
family.intention: We pray for our parish priest and for all who will become priests.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one thing we can leave outside so that we can go through God's door?”

illus: An illustration

In an old house near Kuravilangad the front door was so low that every visitor had to bend to enter. A grandson, tall at fifteen, struck his head on it one Easter holiday and complained. His grandfather laughed and said, “The man who built this house wanted every guest to bow a little before coming in. Even I bow, every day.” Years later the boy, by then a young engineer, told the story in a parish youth meeting on the Gospel of the narrow door: “The door was not too small. I was standing too straight.”

pm.open: Christ is risen! Lord Jesus, our high priest who lives for ever, we gather in your name. Open the door of your word to us tonight. Amen.
share: Not through a legal requirement concerning physical descent, but through the power of an indestructible life (Hebrews 7:16). What does it mean for me that my high priest is alive?
Strive to enter through the narrow door (Luke 13:24). Where is the narrow door in my life this week?
People will come from east and west, from north and south (Luke 13:29). How can our group welcome people who feel far from God?
pm.resp: Risen Lord, bring us in.
interc: For the Church in this season of Qyomtho, that she may welcome all peoples to the table of the kingdom.
For our bishops and priests, that they may serve as men who belong to the eternal priest.
For young men discerning a call to the priesthood.
For those who once ate and drank in the Lord's presence and have drifted away, that they may return.
For all who feel unworthy to approach God, that they may know the door is open to the humble.
pm.close: Father, you made your risen Son our high priest for ever. Through him we approach you with a better hope. Make us humble enough to enter by the narrow door, and gather us with your saints at the banquet of your kingdom. Through Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Christ is the mediator of a new covenant, sealed in his Blood; risen, he himself gives us the inheritance.
Jesus teaches us to take the lowest place, as he did.
Kindness to those who cannot repay is rewarded at the resurrection of the righteous.
2027-04-16.action: Do one kind thing today for someone who cannot repay you.
2027-04-16.question: When I give, am I hoping to be repaid by people, or by God?

family.explain: Jesus was at a big dinner. He saw people rushing to sit in the best seats. He told them: sit in the last seat, and let the host call you up. Then he told the man who gave the dinner: next time, invite poor people, sick people and people who cannot walk or see, who cannot invite you back. God himself will reward you.
family.intention: We pray for families who do not have enough to eat today.
family.ask: Ask: “Whom could our family invite or help this month who cannot pay us back?”

illus: An illustration

A father in Pathanamthitta district was planning his daughter's wedding. The list of guests was long and carefully arranged, and the first sitting of the wedding feast was reserved, as usual, for the important families. A week before the wedding his daughter asked him for one change: that the first sitting be given to the residents of a care home near their parish and to the workers who had built their house. Some relatives were unhappy. On the wedding day the old people were brought in first, and the workers came in clean shirts with their wives. The bride went from table to table serving payasam. Years later, of all the photographs from that day, that is the one the family keeps in the front room.

pm.open: Christ is risen! Lord Jesus, you invite us to your table though we are unworthy. Make us humble and generous like you. Amen.
share: He is the mediator of a new covenant (Hebrews 9:15). What has Jesus' death and Resurrection given me that I could never have earned?
Go and sit down at the lowest place (Luke 14:10). Where do I seek the place of honour?
Invite the poor, the crippled, the lame, and the blind (Luke 14:13). Whom does our group overlook?
pm.resp: Lord, make us humble and generous.
interc: For the Church, that she may always keep the first place at her table for the poor.
For those who are proud of their place and status, that they may learn the way of Jesus.
For the poor, the disabled and the lonely in our parish, that they may be welcomed and honoured.
For families preparing weddings and celebrations, that they may remember those who cannot repay.
For our departed, that they may receive the inheritance promised to those who are called.
pm.close: Father, by the Blood of the new covenant your Son made us your heirs, and by his Resurrection he lives to give us the inheritance. Teach us to take the lowest place and to open our tables to the poor, until we sit with all your saints at the resurrection of the righteous. Through Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Christ offered one sacrifice for all time and sat down at God's right hand; the Holy Qurbono makes that one sacrifice present.
In the new covenant God writes his law on our hearts and remembers our sins no more.
God invites us: “Come; for everything is ready now”; we must not let good things become excuses.
2027-04-17.action: Name tonight one excuse that keeps you from God, and set it aside.
2027-04-17.question: Which good thing in my life has become an excuse for refusing God's invitation?

family.explain: A man prepared a big feast and invited many people. When the food was ready he sent his servant to call them. But they all gave excuses: “I bought a field,” “I bought some oxen,” “I just got married.” So the man invited poor and sick people instead, and there was still room! God invites us every Sunday to the Holy Qurbono. Everything is ready.
family.intention: We pray for those who will miss the Holy Qurbono tomorrow, that they may hear God's invitation.
family.ask: Ask: “What can we do tonight so that nothing stops us from going to church tomorrow?”

illus: An illustration

A young software engineer in Thiruvananthapuram always had a reason for missing the Sunday Qurbono: a release deadline, a new flat to furnish, a cousin's wedding in another town. “Next Sunday,” he would tell his mother on the phone. One Saturday his nephew, who was preparing for his First Holy Communion, called and asked him to come and see him serve at the altar the next morning. He went, a little embarrassed. When the priest lifted up the holy gifts, he found himself thinking of the parable he had once learned in Sunday school: everything is ready now. That evening he went to confession for the first time in four years. He still has deadlines; he no longer lets them decide his Sundays.

pm.open: Christ is risen! Lord Jesus, you have prepared a feast for us and you call us by name. Make us glad to answer your invitation. Amen.
share: Christ had offered for all time a single sacrifice for sins (Hebrews 10:12). How does this change the way I take part in the Holy Qurbono?
I will remember their sins and their lawless deeds no more (Hebrews 10:17). Do I believe that God has truly forgiven me?
But they all alike began to make excuses (Luke 14:18). What are my usual excuses?
pm.resp: Lord, we come; your table is ready.
interc: For the Church, that her invitation may reach the streets and lanes of every town.
For those who have stopped coming to the Holy Qurbono, that they may hear the Lord's call again.
For the poor, the sick and the disabled, that they may find a place of honour at the Lord's table.
For families, that nothing may come before their Sunday worship together.
For all who carry the weight of past sins, that they may trust in God who remembers them no more.
pm.close: Father, your Son offered one sacrifice for all time, and you have set before us the great dinner of your kingdom. Write your law on our hearts, deliver us from every excuse, and fill your house with guests from every road and lane. Through Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Through his flesh Jesus opened a new and living way into God's presence.
We must hold fast to our hope, encourage one another, and not neglect meeting together.
The Good Shepherd seeks the one lost sheep and rejoices when it is found.
2027-04-19.action: Contact one person who has drifted from church and tell them they are missed.
2027-04-19.question: Am I among those who grumble, or among those who go out to seek?

family.explain: A shepherd had a hundred sheep. One got lost. He left the others safe and went looking for the lost one until he found it. Then he carried it home on his shoulders, very happy, and called his friends to a party! Jesus is like that shepherd. When anyone is lost, he looks for them, and heaven is full of joy when they come back.
family.intention: We pray for someone we know who has stopped going to church.
family.ask: Ask: “Who in our family or street might feel lost or left out, and how can we help?”

illus: An illustration

A Sunday school teacher in the Marthandam area noticed that a boy from her class had been absent for three Sundays. Others said, “He will come back when he wants to.” On the fourth Saturday she walked to his house. His father had lost his job, the family was ashamed, and the boy had no clean shirt for Sunday. She said nothing about the absences. The next morning she waited at the church gate, and when the boy came with his mother, she took his hand and walked him to his place in front. Years later the boy, by then a catechist himself, said that he had learned the parable of the lost sheep that morning, without a word of it being read.

pm.open: Christ is risen! Lord Jesus, Good Shepherd, you have opened the way to the Father. Gather us tonight and send us to seek those who are lost. Amen.
share: By the new and living way that he opened for us through the curtain (Hebrews 10:20). What does it mean for me that heaven is open?
Not neglecting to meet together, as is the habit of some (Hebrews 10:25). Why do I need the Sunday assembly, and who needs me there?
He goes after the one that is lost until he finds it (Luke 15:4). Whom is the Lord asking me to seek?
pm.resp: Good Shepherd, seek and save the lost.
interc: For the Church, that she may always go out to seek those who have wandered.
For our parish, that no one may drift away unnoticed.
For young people who have moved away for studies or work, that they may find a home in the Church wherever they are.
For families hurt by quarrels in the parish, that they may be healed and return.
For the sick and the elderly who cannot come to church, that they may receive the Holy Qurbono at home.
pm.close: Father, through the flesh of your Son you have opened for us a new and living way. Make us faithful to the confession of our hope, eager to meet together and encourage one another, and send us with the Good Shepherd to seek the lost. Through Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: We cannot serve God and wealth; money is a servant, not a master.
Jesus restores marriage to God's first plan; the Church upholds it and accompanies the wounded.
Deliberate rejection of Christ's sacrifice leaves no other; but no repented sin is beyond the Church's power to forgive.
2027-04-20.action: Give something today before you spend anything on yourself.
2027-04-20.question: If someone looked at my bank statement and my calendar, whom would they say I serve?

family.explain: Jesus said that nobody can have two bosses at the same time. You cannot serve God and money. Money is useful: we need it for food and school and clothes. But money must never become our boss. God is our only Master, and he wants us to share what we have.
family.intention: We pray for families who are struggling to make ends meet, and for husbands and wives, that they may love each other faithfully.
family.ask: Ask: “How can our family share some of our money or things with someone who needs them this week?”

illus: An illustration

A grocer in Kollam had kept the same shop for thirty years. When his son joined the business, he noticed that the old weighing scale was accurate to the gram and suggested a small adjustment that, he said, every other shop in the market had made. The father took the son to the shrine at the back of the shop, where a small picture of the Sacred Heart hung above the cash box. “This is the one I work for,” he said. “Not the cash box.” The son was annoyed for a few weeks. Years later, when the father died, the queue of customers at the funeral stretched down the road, and many of them said the same thing: “His weight was always true.”

pm.open: Christ is risen! Lord Jesus, you are our only Master. Search our hearts tonight and deliver us from every other master. Amen.
share: You cannot serve God and wealth (Luke 16:13). Where does money compete with God in my life?
God knows your hearts (Luke 16:15). What does God see in my heart that others do not?
It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God (Hebrews 10:31). Do I fear God's hands, or trust them?
pm.resp: Lord, you are our only Master.
interc: For the Church, that she may never be ruled by the love of money, and may be rich in mercy.
For those burdened by debt or tempted by dishonest gain.
For husbands and wives, that they may remain faithful to one another until death.
For those whose marriages have broken down, that they may find compassion and accompaniment in the Church.
For all who have stayed away from confession, that they may trust the mercy of the risen Lord.
pm.close: Father, your Son has shown us that we cannot serve two masters. Make us faithful stewards of what you give us, keep our families united in faithful love, and when we sin, bring us back to your merciful hands. Through Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: The early Church called Baptism enlightenment; we must not abandon the confidence it gave us.
Jesus warns against causing the little ones to stumble and asks us to forgive again and again.
Faith as small as a mustard seed can uproot what seems impossible.
2027-04-21.action: Say the prayer “Lord, increase our faith” ten times today.
2027-04-21.question: Which deep-rooted resentment in me needs a mustard seed of faith?

family.explain: Jesus told his friends: if someone hurts you and then says sorry, forgive them, even seven times in one day! The friends said: that is too hard, Lord, increase our faith! Jesus said that even a tiny faith, as small as a mustard seed, can do great things, like pulling up a big tree by its roots.
family.intention: We pray for anyone we find hard to forgive.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there someone in our family we need to forgive today? Let us do it before we sleep.”

illus: An illustration

Two neighbours in Kottarakkara had not spoken for eleven years over a strip of land between their houses. The quarrel had passed to their children, who walked to the same school on opposite sides of the road. In the Easter season of one year the older of the two men fell ill, and the parish prayer group met in his house. They read this Gospel. When they came to the mustard seed and the mulberry tree, he said quietly, “I have a tree with roots like that.” The next morning he sent his grandson across the road with a plate of appam and a message: “Come and pray with us tonight.” The neighbour came. The land is still there; the quarrel is not.

pm.open: Christ is risen! Lord Jesus, you enlightened us in Baptism. Tonight increase our faith, our endurance and our forgiveness. Amen.
share: Recall those earlier days when, after you had been enlightened (Hebrews 10:32). What do I remember of the time when my faith was most alive?
If the same person sins against you seven times a day... you must forgive (Luke 17:4). Whom do I find it hardest to forgive?
Increase our faith! (Luke 17:5). Where do I need a mustard seed of faith this week?
pm.resp: Lord, increase our faith.
interc: For the Church, that she may endure with confidence in times of trial.
For Christians who suffer persecution or the loss of their goods for the sake of Christ.
For the newly baptized of this Easter, that they may never abandon their confidence.
For children and all the vulnerable, that they may be protected in every home and parish.
For all who carry long resentments, that they may find faith to forgive, through the prayers of St Mary, the holy Mother of God, who kept faith at the foot of the Cross.
pm.close: Father, you enlightened us in Baptism and promised us a great reward. Give us endurance to do your will, hearts that forgive as your Son forgives, and faith enough to uproot every bitterness. Through Jesus Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Hebrews: surrounded by a great cloud of witnesses, we run the race with our eyes fixed on Jesus.
Jesus endured the Cross for the joy set before him; considering him keeps us from losing heart.
The widow kept asking until the judge gave in; how much more will the Father hear his children who cry to him day and night.
2027-04-22.action: Take up again one prayer you had stopped praying, and pray it tonight.
2027-04-22.question: When the Son of Man comes, will he find faith in me?

family.explain: Jesus told a story about a widow who needed help. The judge did not care about anyone, but she kept coming back again and again until he helped her. Jesus says God is much better than that judge: he is our Father and he loves to hear us. So we should keep praying and never give up.
family.intention: We pray for something our family has been asking God for a long time.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one thing we will keep praying for together every night this week?”

illus: An illustration

A grandmother in a parish near Pathanamthitta kept a small notebook beside her Shehimo. On one page she had written the names of her six grandchildren, and every evening, after the evening prayer, she read the names aloud. One grandson had stopped going to church when he left for college in Bengaluru, and for eleven years his name stayed on the page. Her daughter once told her it was no use. She said only: the widow did not stop, so I will not stop. In the twelfth year he came home for Easter, sat at the back of the church and stayed for the whole Qurbono. Afterwards he asked her: Ammachi, were you praying for me? She showed him the notebook.

pm.open: Christ is risen! Lord Jesus, you ran the race before us. Keep our eyes on you and our hearts in prayer. Amen.
share: Since we are surrounded by so great a cloud of witnesses (Hebrews 12:1). Which saint or which person of faith has cheered me on?
Consider him who endured such hostility... so that you may not grow weary (Hebrews 12:3). Where am I growing weary now?
Pray always and not lose heart (Luke 18:1). Which prayer do I need to take up again?
pm.resp: Risen Lord, hear our prayer.
interc: For all who are tired in faith, that they may look again to Jesus and run with perseverance.
For widows and all who have no one to speak for them, that they may find justice.
For judges, lawyers and officials, that they may fear God and respect every person.
For those whose long prayers seem unanswered, that they may not lose heart.
For our parish, that the joy of Qyomtho may become steady, persevering prayer.
pm.close: Father, you never grow tired of hearing your children. Keep us running the race with our eyes on Jesus, keep our prayer alive day and night, and at his coming let him find faith on the earth. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Mar Geevarghese Sahada (St George) was a Christian soldier martyred in the early fourth century; his tomb at Lydda drew pilgrims from early times.
Paul tells Timothy to share in suffering like a good soldier of Christ Jesus, who seeks to please the one who enlisted him.
Jesus sends his witnesses like sheep among wolves, promising that the Spirit of the Father will speak through them.
2027-04-23.action: Pray by name today for one country where Christians are persecuted.
2027-04-23.question: Where is my small daily martyrdom, the place where I must choose Christ against what is easy?
term: The Syriac word for martyr, meaning witness. Our Church gives this title to those who bore witness to Christ by shedding their blood, such as Mar Geevarghese Sahada.
kidsaint: St George was a brave soldier who loved Jesus more than his own life. Long after he died, people told a story about him killing a fierce dragon to save a princess and a whole town. The dragon is a picture of evil and sin. Lesson: whenever you say no to something wrong because you love Jesus, you are fighting the dragon like St George.

family.explain: Today is the feast of Mar Geevarghese, St George. He was a soldier, and when he was told to stop being a Christian, he said no, and he gave his life for Jesus. St Paul says every Christian is like a soldier of Jesus: we stay faithful every day, even when it is hard. Our weapons are prayer, truth and love.
family.intention: We pray for Christians in the world who are hurt or put in prison because they love Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “When is it hard for me to stand up for what is right? How can we help one another?”

illus: An illustration

A young police constable from Kottayam, named Geevarghese after the saint like his grandfather, was posted to a checkpost on a busy highway. In his first month a lorry driver slid a folded note across with his papers. The older men at the post took such notes as a matter of course, and they laughed when he handed it back. For weeks they made his duty hard: the worst shifts, the longest nights. On the feast of his patron he went to the Qurbono before his shift and stood a little longer than usual before the saint's picture. That night he handed back two more notes. Years later one of those older colleagues, near retirement, told him that it was watching him refuse that had made him stop.

pm.open: Christ is risen! Lord Jesus, you made Mar Geevarghese a faithful soldier and a witness of your Resurrection. Make us strong in your grace. Amen.
share: Share in suffering like a good soldier of Christ Jesus (2 Timothy 2:3). What suffering for Christ am I being asked to share?
I am sending you out like sheep into the midst of wolves (Matthew 10:16). Where do I feel like a sheep among wolves?
The one who endures to the end will be saved (Matthew 10:22). What helps me to endure?
pm.resp: By the prayers of Mar Geevarghese, strengthen us, O Lord.
interc: For Christians persecuted for their faith today, that the Spirit may speak through them and keep them faithful.
For soldiers, police and all in uniform, that they may serve with justice and honesty.
For all who bear the name Geevarghese or George, that they may share the courage of their patron.
For those tempted to deny Christ for safety or gain.
For our parish and our Church, that we may be true witnesses of the risen Lord.
pm.close: Father, you crowned Mar Geevarghese with the glory of martyrdom. By his prayers make us good soldiers of Christ, wise and innocent among the wolves of this world, and keep us faithful to the end, so that we may rise with your Son. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: The Pharisee listed his good works and despised others; the tax collector beat his breast and asked for mercy.
The tax collector went home justified: those who humble themselves will be exalted.
Hebrews: the Lord disciplines those he loves, so that we may share his holiness; pursue peace and pull up every root of bitterness.
2027-04-24.action: Make one step of reconciliation before tomorrow's Qurbono.
2027-04-24.question: Where do I most need to ask God for mercy today?

family.explain: Two men went to church to pray. One said: God, look how good I am, much better than that man over there. The other stood at the back, sad for his sins, and said: God, please have mercy on me. Jesus said God was happy with the second man. God loves it when we are honest and say sorry, and he never looks down on us.
family.intention: We pray for anyone in our family or among our friends with whom we have quarrelled, that we may make peace.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there someone I need to say sorry to before Sunday?”

illus: An illustration

A retired headmaster in a parish near Mavelikara was known for his perfect attendance at every Qurbono and every parish meeting. He was also known for his sharp comments about the young people who came late and stood at the back. One Saturday he went for confession and, out of habit, began with the faults of others. The old priest let him finish and then asked quietly: and you, sir? He was silent for a long time. Then he told the priest about a brother he had not spoken to for twenty years over a strip of land. On Sunday he came late for the first time anyone could remember. He had driven to his brother's house first. That morning he stood at the back.

pm.open: Christ is risen! Lord Jesus, we come before you not with our list, but with our need. Have mercy on us. Amen.
share: God, be merciful to me, a sinner! (Luke 18:13). Can I pray this prayer with my whole heart?
The Lord disciplines those whom he loves (Hebrews 12:6). Where has God corrected me, and how has it helped me?
See to it that no root of bitterness springs up (Hebrews 12:15). Is there bitterness in me that I need to bring to God?
pm.resp: Lord, have mercy.
interc: For all who trust in themselves and look down on others, that they may discover the mercy of God.
For those who feel far from God because of their sins, that they may come home like the tax collector.
For families divided by quarrels over property or old wounds, that they may pursue peace.
For priests who hear confessions, that they may be gentle and wise.
For our parish, that we may never despise anyone who comes in through our doors.
pm.close: Father, you humble the proud and exalt the humble. Look on us with mercy, discipline us with love, uproot the bitterness in our hearts, and lead us in the way of peace and holiness, so that we may see you. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Hebrews contrasts Sinai's fire and fear with Mount Zion, the heavenly Jerusalem, where we come to the angels, the saints and Jesus.
The sprinkled blood of Jesus speaks a better word than the blood of Abel: not vengeance, but mercy.
In the parable of the sower the seed is always good; the harvest depends on the soil of our hearts.
2027-04-26.action: Come to your next Qurbono a few minutes early and sit in silence before it begins.
2027-04-26.question: Which kind of soil am I bringing to God's word this week?

family.explain: Jesus told a story about a farmer throwing seeds. Some fell on the hard path and birds ate them. Some fell on rocks and dried up. Some fell among thorns and were choked. But some fell on good soil and grew into a big harvest. The seeds are God's words. Our hearts are the soil. We can make our hearts good soil by listening carefully and remembering what God says.
family.intention: We pray that our hearts may be good soil for God's word.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one thing we heard in church this Sunday? Can we remember it together?”

illus: An illustration

A farmer near Adoor used to plant the same field of tapioca every year, and every year one corner gave almost nothing. His son, home from an agricultural college, dug there and found an old layer of building rubble just under the surface, left from a house that had stood there before his grandfather's time. It took two weekends of hard work with a crowbar to break it up and carry it away. The next season that corner gave the best crop in the field. The farmer said afterwards that he had blamed the seed for twenty years, when the trouble had been under his feet all along.

pm.open: Christ is risen! Lord Jesus, sower of the word, open our ears and soften our hearts to receive you. Amen.
share: You have come to Mount Zion... and to innumerable angels in festal gathering (Hebrews 12:22). How do I usually come to the Qurbono?
The sprinkled blood that speaks a better word than the blood of Abel (Hebrews 12:24). What word does the blood of Jesus speak to me?
Other seed fell into good soil and brought forth grain (Mark 4:8). What are the thorns that choke God's word in me?
pm.resp: Lord, make us good soil.
interc: For all who preach and teach the word of God, that they may sow generously and faithfully.
For those whose hearts have become hard, that the word may break through.
For those whose faith has no root, that they may grow deep in prayer.
For those choked by worries and riches, that the Lord may release them.
For farmers and all who work the land, that their labour may be blessed with a good harvest.
pm.close: Father, your Son has brought us to Mount Zion and sown in us the seed of eternal life. Make our hearts good soil, let us listen with reverence and joy, and bring forth in us the fruit of your word. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Hebrews: God will shake earth and heaven so that what cannot be shaken may remain; we are receiving an unshakable kingdom, and we respond with thankful worship.
The rich ruler went away sad because he was very rich; Jesus promises much more to those who leave everything for the kingdom.
St Cletus, an early Bishop of Rome after St Peter, faithfully handed on what he had received.
2027-04-27.action: Give away one thing you are attached to, to someone who needs it.
2027-04-27.question: What am I holding on to that could be shaken away in a night?

family.explain: A rich man asked Jesus how to live forever with God. Jesus said: give your riches to the poor and come, follow me. But the man was sad because he loved his things too much. Peter said: we left everything to follow you! And Jesus promised that God gives back much more to people who follow him. Things can break or be lost, but God's kingdom lasts forever.
family.intention: We pray for people who lost their homes in floods, fires or wars.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one thing in our house we could give to someone who needs it more?”

illus: An illustration

In August 2018 a family near Chengannur lost almost everything to the flood. When the water went down, the father walked through the house: the furniture was ruined, the photographs gone, the car useless. In a high cupboard he found the family Bible and the small cross his mother had kept, both dry. That evening the family, staying in a relief camp in the parish hall, prayed the evening prayer with the cross propped on a chair. The youngest daughter asked why they were thanking God when they had lost so much. Her father said: we are all alive, we are all together, and God is still God. That is what the water could not take.

pm.open: Christ is risen! Lord Jesus, you give us a kingdom that cannot be shaken. Loosen our grip on what passes. Amen.
share: See that you do not refuse the one who is speaking (Hebrews 12:25). Where is God speaking to me now, and am I listening?
There is still one thing lacking (Luke 18:22). What is the one thing still lacking in me?
Look, we have left our homes and followed you (Luke 18:28). What have I left for Christ, and what has he given back?
pm.resp: Lord, be our treasure.
interc: For all who have lost homes and possessions in floods, fires and wars, that they may find help and hope.
For the rich, that they may be generous and detached in heart.
For the Pope, the successor of St Peter and St Cletus, and for our Major Archbishop-Catholicos and bishops.
For priests, religious and missionaries who have left home and family for the kingdom.
For our parish, that we may give thanks with reverence and awe at every Qurbono.
pm.close: Father, in your Son you give us a kingdom that cannot be shaken. Release us from all that holds us back, keep your Church firm on the faith of the apostles, and let us offer you a worship of thanks with reverence and awe. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Hebrews: remember your leaders who spoke God's word to you, and imitate their faith; Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever.
We have an altar: the sacrifice of Christ, from which flow the sacrifice of praise and the sacrifice of doing good and sharing.
The faithful and wise servant gives the household its food at the proper time and is found at work when the master comes.
2027-04-28.action: Pray for a priest, bishop or catechist who taught you the faith and has died.
2027-04-28.question: In the household God has entrusted to me, am I giving food at the proper time?

family.explain: Today our Church remembers a bishop, Isaac Mar Yoohanon, who died forty years ago. The Bible tells us to remember the people who taught us about God and to copy their faith. Jesus also tells a story about a good servant whose master put him in charge of feeding the whole house. The servant did his job faithfully, and the master was very happy. Each of us has a job from God: helping at home, doing homework, being kind to brothers and sisters.
family.intention: We pray for the bishops and priests who have died, and for our bishops and priests today.
family.ask: Ask: “Who taught each of us about Jesus? Let us thank God for them by name.”

illus: An illustration

An imagined story, about another bishop whose name is not given. In a parish near Thiruvalla the old sacristy cupboard held a worn black leather case with a chalice inside. One day a young altar server asked why it was kept there when the parish had newer chalices. The vicar told him that a bishop had used it when he came to the village on foot during the monsoon, many decades ago, to celebrate the Qurbono in a church with a thatched roof. The bishop had baptized the vicar's own grandfather. On the bishop's memorial day the vicar used that chalice. The boy served at that Qurbono, and afterwards he said he had felt as if the whole line of them were standing behind him: the bishop, the grandfather, the priests in between.

pm.open: Christ is risen! Lord Jesus, you are the same yesterday and today and forever. We thank you for the shepherds who gave us the faith. Amen.
share: Remember your leaders... and imitate their faith (Hebrews 13:7). Whose faith do I want to imitate?
Let us continually offer a sacrifice of praise to God (Hebrews 13:15). Is praise a daily part of my life?
Blessed is that slave whom his master will find at work when he arrives (Matthew 24:46). What work has the Lord entrusted to me?
pm.resp: Lord, give rest to your servants and strength to your Church.
interc: For the soul of Most Rev. Isaac Mar Yoohanon and all the departed bishops, priests and religious of our Church.
For our Major Archbishop-Catholicos, our bishops and priests, that they may be faithful and wise stewards.
For parents, teachers and all who are responsible for others, that they may give food at the proper time.
For those who have no lasting city: refugees, migrants and the homeless.
For our parish, that our worship at the altar may become praise on our lips and generosity in our hands.
pm.close: Father, your Son is the same yesterday and today and forever. Grant eternal rest to the shepherds who served your people, give your Church faithful stewards in every age, and make us ready to be found at work when he comes. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Five bridesmaids took oil with their lamps and five did not; only those who were ready went in to the wedding banquet.
Paul prays that the God of peace may sanctify us entirely, spirit, soul and body: the one who calls us is faithful.
St Catherine of Siena (1347–1380), Doctor of the Church, burned with prayer and love for the Church and the Pope.
2027-04-29.action: Spend fifteen minutes in quiet prayer today, before the Blessed Sacrament if possible.
2027-04-29.question: What is the oil I need to buy now, before the Bridegroom comes?

family.explain: Ten girls were waiting with lamps for a bridegroom so that they could go to the wedding party. Five brought extra oil, and five did not. The bridegroom came late at night. The girls without oil had to go and buy some, and when they came back the door was shut. Jesus wants us always to be ready for him. We fill our lamps with love when we pray, go to church and are kind to others. St Catherine of Siena was a girl who loved Jesus so much that her lamp was always full.
family.intention: We pray for the Pope and for the whole Church, as St Catherine did.
family.ask: Ask: “What can each of us do this week to keep our lamp full of love?”

illus: An illustration

A nurse from Kottayam working night shifts in a hospital in the Gulf kept a small oil lamp on the shelf of her shared room. She could not light it there, so she kept it unlit and said a short prayer every time she looked at it: Lord, keep my lamp full. Her roommates, of other faiths, sometimes asked about it. One night, after a patient she had cared for for weeks died on her shift, she came home exhausted and sat on her bed in tears. One of her roommates quietly took the little lamp down from the shelf and put it in her hands, saying: you told me this is for when you are empty. They sat together till dawn. The nurse said later that it was the first time she had understood that the oil was not her own strength.

pm.open: Christ is risen! Lord Jesus, risen Bridegroom, keep our lamps burning until you come. Amen.
share: The wise took flasks of oil with their lamps (Matthew 25:4). What is the oil in my life, and is it running low?
May the God of peace himself sanctify you entirely (1 Thessalonians 5:23). Which part of my life have I kept back from God's holiness?
Beloved, pray for us (1 Thessalonians 5:25). Whom do I need to ask for prayer, and for whom must I pray?
pm.resp: Lord, keep our lamps burning.
interc: For the Church throughout the world, that she may be a bride ready for her Lord.
For the Pope and all bishops, that St Catherine's prayers may give them courage and wisdom.
For women who give their lives in prayer and service, especially consecrated women.
For nurses and all who care for the sick through the night.
For those whose lamps of faith are going out, that the faithful God may renew them.
pm.close: Father, your Son is the Bridegroom who will come at midnight. By the prayers of St Catherine of Siena, fill us with the oil of love, sanctify us entirely, and keep us awake and ready to enter the banquet of the Lamb. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Mar Yaqob Shleeha, St James son of Zebedee, brother of John, was one of the three closest disciples and the first apostle to be martyred (Acts 12:2).
James and John asked for the seats of glory; Jesus offered them his cup and taught that greatness is service.
Paul: restore the fallen gently, bear one another's burdens, and do not grow weary in doing good.
2027-04-30.action: Do one hidden act of service today for someone who cannot repay you.
2027-04-30.question: Am I asking Jesus for a throne, or for a share in his cup?
term: The Syriac word for apostle, meaning one who is sent. Our Church gives this title to the Twelve and to St Paul, as in Mar Yaqob Shleeha, St James the Apostle.
kidsaint: James was a fisherman who left his boat to follow Jesus. He and his brother John were so full of energy that Jesus called them sons of thunder! Once they asked Jesus for the best seats in heaven, but Jesus taught them that the greatest person is the one who serves others. James learned, and he gave his life for Jesus. Lesson: being great means helping others, not being first.

family.explain: James and his brother John asked Jesus if they could have the most important seats next to him. The other disciples were cross with them. Jesus said: in my family, the greatest is the one who serves everyone. I came to serve, not to be served. James understood, and later he gave his life for Jesus. Today is his feast.
family.intention: We pray for all who serve others: parents, nurses, cleaners, drivers, and all who work quietly for others.
family.ask: Ask: “How can each of us serve someone at home this week without being asked?”

illus: An illustration

In a large joint family near Kollam, the eldest son had always expected the best seat at the table and the last word in every decision. When his father fell ill and needed care through the night, the family made a rota. The eldest son's name was not on it; no one dared to ask him. One night his younger sister, exhausted after a week of nights, found him already sitting by their father's bed with a basin of water and a towel. He kept the night shift for the rest of their father's illness. After the funeral he told the parish priest that those were the nights he had first felt like a son, and not only the eldest.

pm.open: Christ is risen! Lord Jesus, you came to serve and to give your life for us. By the prayers of Mar Yaqob Shleeha, make us servants of one another. Amen.
share: Grant us to sit, one at your right hand and one at your left (Mark 10:37). What places of honour do I secretly want?
Whoever wishes to become great among you must be your servant (Mark 10:43). Whom am I being asked to serve?
Bear one another's burdens (Galatians 6:2). Whose burden can I help to carry?
pm.resp: By the prayers of Mar Yaqob Shleeha, make us servants, O Lord.
interc: For the Pope, bishops and priests, that they may lead by serving, as the apostles learned to do.
For those who have fallen into sin, that they may be restored with gentleness.
For all who carry heavy burdens alone, that they may find others to help them.
For those tempted to give up doing good, that they may not grow weary.
For all who bear the name of St James, and for pilgrims on the road to his shrine.
pm.close: Father, your Son came not to be served but to serve. By the prayers of Mar Yaqob, the first of the apostles to drink his cup, teach us to serve one another, to bear one another's burdens, and to persevere in doing good until the harvest. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, on the evening of Easter the disciples were behind locked doors, full of fear. Jesus came and stood among them: “Peace be with you.” He showed them his wounds. Then he sent them: “As the Father has sent me, so I send you.” He breathed on them: “Receive the Holy Spirit. If you forgive the sins of any, they are forgiven.”

Thomas was not there, and he would not believe: “Unless I see the marks of the nails and put my hand in his side, I will not believe.” A week later Jesus came again and invited him: “Put your finger here; reach out your hand. Do not doubt, but believe.” And Thomas cried out: “My Lord and my God!”

Dear friends, this is our own family story. Thomas, who doubted and then believed, brought this faith to India. We are called St Thomas Christians. His doubt, healed by the wounds of Christ, became our faith. In many of our churches people whisper his words when the priest lifts up the holy Mysteries: My Lord and my God.
