Jesus then said: “Blessed are those who have not seen and yet have come to believe.” That is you and me. We have not seen him, but we love him. Let us not live behind locked doors of fear. Let us bring our doubts to his wounds, receive his peace, and go out as witnesses. My Lord and my God! Amen.
kids: Children, after Jesus rose, Thomas said: “I won't believe unless I see him myself!”
A week later Jesus came and said: “Thomas, look at my hands.” Thomas fell down and said: “My Lord and my God!”
Thomas later came to India to tell people about Jesus. That's why we are St Thomas Christians! Let's say together: “My Lord and my God!”

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, after Easter Peter says, “I am going fishing,” and six others go with him. They work all night and catch nothing. Many of us know such nights: hard work with nothing to show for it, prayers that seem unanswered, plans that fail.

At dawn a stranger calls from the shore: “Cast the net to the right side.” They do, and the net is full. John cries, “It is the Lord!” and Peter jumps into the water. On the beach Jesus has a fire going, with fish and bread. “Come and have breakfast.” The risen Lord cooks for his tired friends. That is our God: he meets us in our failures and feeds us.

After breakfast, beside the fire, Jesus asks Peter three times: “Do you love me?” Three times, because three times Peter had denied him by another fire. Jesus does not scold him; he lets love heal the wound. “Lord, you know that I love you.” “Feed my sheep.” Peter, forgiven, is made the shepherd of the Church.

Whatever your failures, Jesus asks you the same question today: “Do you love me?” Answer him honestly. And let your love become service: feed his lambs, in your family, your parish, your work. Every Holy Qurbono he says again: “Come and have breakfast.” Amen.
kids: Children, the disciples went fishing all night and caught nothing. In the morning a man on the beach said: “Throw your net on the right side!” And the net was full of fish!
It was Jesus! He had made breakfast for them on the beach. Then he asked Peter: “Do you love me?” Peter said: “Yes, Lord, you know I love you!”
Jesus asks you too: “Do you love me?” What will you say? Let's say: “Jesus, I love you!”

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, on Easter afternoon two disciples are walking away from Jerusalem, sad and disappointed. “We had hoped that he was the one,” they say. Many of us walk such roads: disappointed with life, with the Church, with God. And then a stranger joins them.

It is Jesus, but they do not recognise him. He lets them pour out their sorrow. Then he opens the Scriptures, from Moses and all the prophets, and shows them that the Messiah had to suffer and enter his glory. Later they will say: “Were not our hearts burning within us while he was opening the scriptures?”

As evening falls they invite him in: “Stay with us.” At table he takes bread, blesses it, breaks it and gives it to them, and their eyes are opened. This is exactly what happens at every Holy Qurbono: the Word sets our hearts on fire; the breaking of the bread opens our eyes. Emmaus is not just a story; it is our Sunday.

And they could not keep it to themselves. In the dark they ran back seven miles to Jerusalem to tell the others: “The Lord is risen!” Let us read the Gospel each day this week, invite Jesus into our homes, and tell someone what he has done for us. Stay with us, Lord. Amen.
kids: Children, two friends of Jesus were walking home, very sad. A stranger walked with them and explained the Bible. Their hearts felt warm!
At supper the stranger broke the bread, and suddenly they saw: it was Jesus! Then he disappeared.
They ran all the way back to tell their friends! When the priest breaks the bread at Qurbana, Jesus is there too. Let's say: “Jesus, stay with us!”

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, the disciples are gathered, frightened and confused, when the risen Jesus stands among them: “Peace be with you. Why are you frightened? Look at my hands and my feet; it is I myself.” He even eats a piece of fish in front of them. The Resurrection is not a ghost story; the Lord is truly alive, body and soul.

Then he opens their minds to understand the Scriptures, and gives them a task: repentance and forgiveness of sins must be proclaimed in his name to all nations. “You are witnesses of these things.” In Matthew he says it on a mountain: “Go therefore and make disciples of all nations… And remember, I am with you always.”

This command is not only for priests and sisters. St Paul says every Christian is “an ambassador for Christ”. Today our Church honours the laity, because most of the world will never hear a sermon from a priest; they will only see Christ in you: in your honesty at work, your patience at home, your kindness to the poor, your courage to say “I am a Christian.”

Job was restored when he prayed for his friends. Solomon received wisdom when he asked. Let us ask the risen Lord for wisdom and courage, and go out from this Qurbono as his witnesses. He has promised: “I am with you always, to the end of the age.” Amen.
kids: Children, before Jesus went back to heaven, he gave his friends a big job: “Go and tell everyone about me!”
And he made a promise: “I will be with you always.” Jesus is with us every day, at school, at home, everywhere.
You can tell others about Jesus by being kind and honest. Let's say: “Jesus, I will be your helper!”

homily: Dear friends, Christ is risen! In today's Gospel some Sadducees, who say there is no resurrection, bring Jesus a story about seven brothers and one wife. They want to make the hope of rising look foolish.

Jesus answers gently but clearly: you are wrong, because you know neither the Scriptures nor the power of God (Mark 12:24). The life to come is not this life repeated. It is the life of God, where every faithful love is fulfilled.

Then he reminds them of the burning bush: I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob. God is not the God of the dead, but of the living. The patriarchs were alive to him. The Letter to the Hebrews adds: we do see Jesus, crowned with glory and honor because he tasted death for everyone (Hebrews 2:9).
So in this Hevoro week, let us speak of our departed with Easter hope, pray for them at the Holy Qurbono, and live as people who believe that God is the God of the living. Amen.
kids: Children, Christ is risen! Some people asked Jesus a tricky question because they did not believe that people who die will live again. Jesus said: God is the God of the living! Abraham, who lived long, long ago, is alive to God. Jesus rose at Easter, and one day he will raise us too. Tonight, can you pray for someone in your family who has gone to God?

homily: Dear friends, Christ is risen! On this first Friday after Qyomtho our Church remembers all the confessors: those who confessed Christ before others and paid for it with prison, exile or death. The Letter to the Hebrews calls them people of whom the world was not worthy (Hebrews 11:38).

Why did they stand firm? The Lord tells us in the Gospel. Do not fear those who kill the body but cannot kill the soul. Not a sparrow falls without your Father; even the hairs of your head are counted. So do not be afraid; you are of more value than many sparrows (Matthew 10:31).

And he gives a promise: Everyone who acknowledges me before others, I also will acknowledge before my Father in heaven (Matthew 10:32). In this white week we see the confessors, with Revelation, robed in white, their robes washed in the blood of the Lamb.

Let us pray today for Christians who suffer for the faith, ask the Virgin Mary, Queen of Confessors, for courage, and make our own small confessions: a sign of the cross, a word for Christ, a Sunday kept holy. The risen Lord does not forget them. Amen.
kids: Children, Christ is risen! Today we remember all the brave Christians who said “I belong to Jesus,” even when people hurt them for it. Jesus said: do not be afraid! God looks after every little sparrow, and he even knows how many hairs are on your head. Can you be brave for Jesus today, maybe by making the sign of the cross before you eat?

homily: Dear friends, Christ is risen! On this last day of Hevoro week the Letter to the Hebrews says: consider Jesus, the apostle and high priest of our confession (Hebrews 3:1). He is sent to us from the Father, and he goes for us to the Father.

Moses was faithful in God's house as a servant; Christ is faithful over God's house as a son. And then a beautiful line: we are his house, if we hold firm the confidence and the pride that belong to hope (Hebrews 3:6). The Church is not first a building of stones; we are the house of God.

In the Gospel John wants to stop a man who casts out demons in Jesus' name, because he does not follow with us. Jesus says: Do not stop him; whoever is not against you is for you (Luke 9:50). The house of God is larger than our little circle. We hold the fullness of the faith with gratitude, and we rejoice in every good done in his name.
Tomorrow is New Sunday. Let us hold firm our hope, thank God for good done by others, go to confession if we can, and come ready to say with Thomas: My Lord and my God. Amen.
kids: Children, Christ is risen! Do you know that you are God's house? Not a house made of bricks, but a house made of people who love Jesus. One day John tried to stop a man doing good in Jesus' name because he was not in their group. Jesus said: do not stop him! Jesus is happy whenever anyone does good. Who can you say thank you to today for doing something good?

homily: Dear friends, Christ is risen! Today St Paul writes from prison: Remember Jesus Christ, raised from the dead, a descendant of David (2 Timothy 2:8). He is chained like a criminal, yet he says: the word of God is not chained.

Then he gives us a sure saying: if we have died with him, we will also live with him; if we endure, we will also reign with him. And the most comforting line: if we are faithless, he remains faithful, for he cannot deny himself (2 Timothy 2:13).

In the Gospel Jesus tells of a vineyard and a beloved son who is killed and thrown out. He is speaking of himself. The warning is for every steward of God's vineyard in every age, including us. And the parable ends with Easter: the stone that the builders rejected has become the cornerstone (Mark 12:10).

So let us remember Jesus Christ, raised from the dead, when we wake and when we sleep; let us give God his share of the vineyard he has given us; and if we have been faithless, let us return to him who remains faithful. Amen.
kids: Children, Christ is risen! St Paul was in prison, but he wrote: remember Jesus Christ, raised from the dead! Nobody could lock up the good news about Jesus. Jesus also told a story about a stone that builders threw away, but it became the most important stone of the whole house. That is what God did at Easter. Tonight before you sleep, can you say: Jesus, you are risen?

homily: Dear friends, Christ is risen! St Paul tells us today what Easter has already done in us. You were dead through your trespasses. But God, who is rich in mercy, out of the great love with which he loved us, made us alive together with Christ (Ephesians 2:4–5).

By grace you have been saved through faith; it is the gift of God. And then: we are what he has made us, created in Christ Jesus for good works (Ephesians 2:10). Grace is pure gift, and grace makes us able to love.

In the Gospel Jesus enters Simon's house, stands over the sick woman, and rebukes the fever. Immediately she got up and began to serve them (Luke 4:39). At sunset he lays his hands on each of the sick and heals them. He knows each one by name.
So let us thank God for our Baptism, ask him to rebuke whatever fever burns in us, and rise at once to serve. Let us bring our sick to him at this Holy Qurbono. Amen.
kids: Children, Christ is risen! One day Jesus went to Peter's house, and Peter's mother-in-law was very sick with a fever. Jesus told the fever to go away, and it did! At once she got up and made food for everyone. When Jesus helps us, we can help others too. What can you do to help at home today?

homily: Dear friends, Christ is risen! On Easter evening the Lord said to his disciples, Peace be with you. Today St Paul tells us how deep that peace goes: he is our peace; in his flesh he has made both groups into one and has broken down the dividing wall, that is, the hostility between us (Ephesians 2:14).

We who were far off have been brought near by the blood of Christ, brought into the hope of Israel's covenants. Through him all of us have access in one Spirit to the Father. Christ has already broken the wall. Our part is to stop rebuilding it in our families, our parishes, and between Churches.

In the Gospel Jesus says that no one hides a lamp under a jar. The light of Easter is not for hiding. And he adds: pay attention to how you listen (Luke 8:18). The one who listens with faith receives more.
So this week let us take one step across a wall: a greeting, a call, a visit, a prayer for someone by name. And let us listen to God's word as if for the first time. Amen.
kids: Children, Christ is risen! St Paul says that Jesus is our peace. When people are angry with each other, it is like building a wall between them. Jesus came to break down walls, so that we can all be friends in God's family. Is there someone you had a fight with? Today you can say sorry, or just say hello with a smile.

homily: Dear friends, Christ is risen! Today the Letter to the Hebrews says: remember your leaders, those who spoke the word of God to you; consider the outcome of their way of life, and imitate their faith (Hebrews 13:7). The Panchangam remembers today Most Rev. Lawrence Mar Ephrem, a bishop of our Church who died in 1997.

Shepherds come and go, but Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever (Hebrews 13:8). Every shepherd who served us faithfully handed on the one risen Lord, who does not change. That is why we pray for our departed bishops and give thanks for them.

The Gospel asks: who then is the faithful and wise slave, whom his master has put in charge of his household, to give the other slaves their allowance of food at the proper time? (Matthew 24:45). Every bishop, priest, parent and teacher is such a steward. The food the household needs most is the word of God and the Bread of life.

We have an altar, says Hebrews: the sacrifice of Christ, made present in the Holy Qurbono. From that altar let us go out to offer God a sacrifice of praise, to do good and to share what we have. May the risen Lord find each of us at work when he comes. Amen.
kids: Children, Christ is risen! Do you remember who taught you to make the sign of the Cross, or to pray the Our Father? Maybe a grandmother, a teacher or a priest. Today the Bible says: remember the people who told you about God, and try to be like them. Tonight, say thank you to God for one of those people, and say a prayer for them.

homily: Dear friends, Christ is risen! Today St Paul tells his own story: I was violently persecuting the church of God and was trying to destroy it (Galatians 1:13). Then God, who had set him apart before he was born, was pleased to reveal his Son to him.
Paul did not rush to the front. He went to Arabia, returned to Damascus, and only after three years went to visit Cephas. Conversion needs hidden time with God.

And the churches of Judea heard: the one who formerly was persecuting us is now proclaiming the faith he once tried to destroy. And they glorified God because of me (Galatians 1:23–24). A changed life is a witness to the Resurrection.
In the Gospel Jesus puts a little child by his side: the least among all of you is the greatest (Luke 9:48). Let us pray for someone we have given up on, and welcome the least in his name. Amen.
kids: Children, Christ is risen! Once there was a man named Saul who hurt the friends of Jesus. Then Jesus, alive and full of light, met him on the road. Saul became St Paul, one of the greatest friends Jesus ever had. Nobody is too bad for Jesus to love and change. Can you pray today for someone who is unkind to you?

homily: Dear friends, Christ is risen! After fourteen years of preaching, St Paul went up to Jerusalem and laid his gospel before the leaders of the Church, in order to make sure that I was not running, or had not run, in vain (Galatians 2:2). Even a great apostle does not run alone.
He defended the freedom we have in Christ: Titus was not compelled to be circumcised. We are saved by the grace of the risen Lord, and God shows no partiality (Galatians 2:6).
In the Gospel Jesus grieves: woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! They saw his mighty works and did not repent. We too have seen much this Easter. Have we changed?

Whoever listens to you listens to me (Luke 10:16). Christ speaks through his Church. Like the holy Mother of God, who kept the word in her heart, let us listen, and let his word change something in us this week. Amen.
kids: Children, Christ is risen! Jesus once said to his friends: when people listen to you, they are listening to me. So when your parents or your Sunday school teacher tell you about Jesus, it is really Jesus speaking to you. Listening means doing what we hear. What will you do this week that Jesus asks?

homily: Dear friends, Christ is risen! The first word of the risen Lord to his disciples was peace. St Paul tells us what it means: since we are justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ (Romans 5:1). We stand in grace, unafraid.

Even suffering is changed. Suffering produces endurance, and endurance produces character, and character produces hope, and hope does not disappoint us, because God's love has been poured into our hearts through the Holy Spirit (Romans 5:3–5).

Today we remember St Julius, Pope. When St Athanasius was driven out of Alexandria for defending the faith that the Son is truly God, Julius welcomed him in Rome and stood up for him. Whoever welcomes you welcomes me, says Jesus (Matthew 10:40).
Welcome is within everyone's reach: even a cup of cold water given in his name will not lose its reward. Let us give someone that cup this week: a meal, a visit, a word of welcome. Amen.
kids: Children, Christ is risen! Jesus said that if we give even a glass of cold water to someone in his name, God will never forget it. Long ago Pope Julius welcomed a bishop who had been chased away. Can you welcome someone this week, maybe a new child in your class? When you welcome them, you are welcoming Jesus!

homily: Dear friends, Christ is risen! Hebrews says: in the days of his flesh, Jesus offered up prayers and supplications, with loud cries and tears, to the one who was able to save him from death, and he was heard (Hebrews 5:7).
He was not spared the Cross, but he was heard: the Father brought him through death into the Resurrection. When we pray with tears, we are not alone. The Son has prayed this way before us.

Christ did not make himself a priest. The Father said to him, You are a priest forever, according to the order of Melchizedek. Risen and alive, he offers himself for us at every Holy Qurbono and always lives to intercede for us.
The disciples said, Lord, teach us to pray, and Jesus gave them the Our Father. Let us pray it slowly today, forgive those who have hurt us, and trust the Father who heard his Son. Amen.
kids: Children, Christ is risen! One day the disciples saw Jesus praying and said, Lord, teach us to pray. So Jesus taught them the Our Father. Do you know it by heart? Tonight, say it very slowly with your family, and think about each word. Jesus is teaching you to talk to God as your own Father!

homily: Dear friends, Christ is risen! Hebrews says: let us go on toward perfection (Hebrews 6:1). The feast of Easter is not an end. The foundation of faith has been laid in us; now the Lord wants to build.

Ground that drinks up the rain falling on it repeatedly, and that produces a crop useful to those for whom it is cultivated, receives a blessing from God (Hebrews 6:7). Easter is rain on our lives. Let it bear fruit.

Today we remember Mar Shemun Bar Sabbae, bishop of Seleucia-Ctesiphon in Persia. He refused to burden his poor people and to worship the sun, and he died a martyr on a Good Friday in the fourth century. An official who had denied Christ was moved by his courage, came back to the faith and died a martyr too.

Where does such strength come from? From prayer. Ask, and it will be given you; search, and you will find; knock, and the door will be opened for you. How much more will the heavenly Father give the Holy Spirit to those who ask him! Let us ask every day until Pentecost. Amen.
kids: Children, Christ is risen! Jesus told a story about a man who knocked on his friend's door at midnight and kept knocking until his friend gave him bread. Jesus says: keep asking God! He is a good Father, and he loves to give us the Holy Spirit. Every night this week, say this little prayer: Father, give me your Holy Spirit.

homily: Dear friends, Christ is risen! Today the Letter to the Hebrews tells us that Jesus is not a priest because of the family he was born into. He became a priest through the power of an indestructible life (Hebrews 7:16).

That is the Easter mystery. The life that death could not destroy is the root of his priesthood. A priest who dies needs someone to take his place; our high priest lives for ever and always intercedes for us.

In the Gospel someone asks, “Lord, will only a few be saved?” Jesus answers: strive to enter through the narrow door (Luke 13:24). Some will say, “We ate and drank with you,” and still stand outside. Being near the Lord is not yet the same as entering by him. The door is narrow for the proud and wide for the humble.

And yet the promise is wide: people will come from east and west and eat in the kingdom of God. We have come from the east. Let us enter by the door who is Christ: in humble confession, in faithful coming to the Holy Qurbono, in daily love. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus is alive, and he is our priest for ever! Someone asked him how many people would go to heaven. Jesus said: try hard to go in through the narrow door. To pass through a low, narrow door you have to bend down. That is what humble people do. Can you do one humble thing today, like saying sorry first or letting someone else go first?

homily: Dear friends, Christ is risen! The Letter to the Hebrews says that Jesus is the mediator of a new covenant, so that those who are called may receive the promised eternal inheritance (Hebrews 9:15).

A will takes effect only after death. Christ died, and his will is in force: forgiveness, adoption, eternal life. But this testator rose again on the third day. He himself gives us what he left us, especially his own Body and Blood in the Holy Qurbono.

In the Gospel Jesus watches the guests choosing the best seats, and he says: go and sit down at the lowest place (Luke 14:10). That is his own way. He took the lowest place on the Cross, and the Father raised him up. Then he tells the host to invite the poor, the crippled, the lame and the blind, because they cannot repay, and you will be repaid at the resurrection of the righteous (Luke 14:14).
Because Christ is risen, no unreturned kindness is wasted. This week let us take a lower seat gladly, and invite to our table someone who cannot invite us back. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus once saw people pushing to get the best chairs at a party. He said: go and sit in the last chair, and the host will call you up! He also said: when you have a party, invite people who are poor or sick, who cannot invite you back. God will reward you. Can you share something today with someone who cannot give you anything in return?

homily: Dear friends, Christ is risen! The Letter to the Hebrews contrasts the priests who stand day after day offering the same sacrifices with Christ, who offered for all time a single sacrifice for sins and sat down at the right hand of God (Hebrews 10:12).

He sits because his work is finished. The Holy Qurbono does not add to the Cross; it makes the one sacrifice present, and the risen Lord gives himself to us. And in this new covenant God says: I will remember their sins and their lawless deeds no more.

In the Gospel a man gives a great dinner and says: Come; for everything is ready now (Luke 14:17). But the guests make excuses: a field, oxen, a marriage. Good things, put in the place of the invitation. So the master calls the poor, the crippled, the blind and the lame, and still there is room.
Tonight Sunday begins. Everything is ready for us tomorrow: the Word, the Body and Blood of Christ, his peace. Let us lay aside our excuses, prepare our hearts, and bring someone with us. Amen.
kids: Children, imagine someone made a huge feast with all your favourite food, and invited you, and you said: “Sorry, I'm busy.” In Jesus' story people said exactly that! So the man invited poor and sick people, and the house was filled. Every Sunday Jesus invites us to his feast, the Holy Qurbono. Will you say “Yes, I am coming!” tomorrow?

homily: Dear friends, Christ is risen! The Letter to the Hebrews says that Jesus opened for us a new and living way through the curtain, that is, through his flesh (Hebrews 10:20). At his death the curtain of the temple was torn. Heaven is open.

So we are told: let us hold fast to the confession of our hope without wavering, for he who has promised is faithful (Hebrews 10:23). Let us encourage one another, and not neglect to meet together, as is the habit of some.

In the Gospel the shepherd leaves the ninety-nine and goes after the one that is lost until he finds it. He does not scold; he lays it on his shoulders and rejoices. St Ambrose saw in those shoulders the arms of the Cross (in substance).

Yesterday we heard how the Emmaus disciples ran back to the community. Today let us look for those who have not come back. Call one of them; visit; bring them with you. And if you are the lost one, know that the Shepherd is already on the road looking for you. Amen.
kids: Children, have you ever lost something you loved and searched everywhere for it? Jesus told a story about a shepherd who lost one sheep. He searched and searched until he found it, then carried it home on his shoulders and had a party! Jesus loves every one of us like that. If a friend stops coming to Sunday school, can you tell them: we miss you?

homily: Dear friends, Christ is risen! Today Jesus says plainly: no slave can serve two masters... You cannot serve God and wealth (Luke 16:13). Money is a good servant and a poor master. It asks for the whole heart, and so does God.

St John Chrysostom said that not to share our goods with the poor is to steal from them, for what we hold is also theirs (in substance). The risen Lord asks us to use what passes so as to gain what lasts.

Jesus also restores marriage to the beginning: what God has joined, no one may separate. The Church holds this firmly, and she is also asked to accompany with love those whose marriages have broken, many of whom were hurt against their will.

The Letter to the Hebrews warns: it is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God. But the fearful thing is to refuse his mercy. On Easter evening Jesus gave the apostles power to forgive sins. Like King David, let us choose to fall into the hand of the Lord, for his mercy is great. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus said: nobody can have two bosses. You cannot serve God and money. Money is useful, but God must always be number one. Can you think of one thing you could share today, a sweet, a toy, a coin, with someone who has less? When we share, we show that God is our boss, not money.

homily: Dear friends, Christ is risen! The Letter to the Hebrews says: recall those earlier days when, after you had been enlightened, you endured a hard struggle with sufferings (Hebrews 10:32). The early Church called Baptism enlightenment.

Those first Christians had suffered, been mocked, lost their possessions, and still rejoiced, knowing they had something better and more lasting. Now some were growing tired. So the Letter says: do not, therefore, abandon that confidence of yours; it brings a great reward (Hebrews 10:35).

In the Gospel Jesus asks us to protect the little ones and to forgive, even seven times a day. The apostles reply: Increase our faith! They knew that only faith can forgive like that. Jesus answers that faith the size of a mustard seed can uproot a mulberry tree, the deep roots of an old resentment.
Let us thank God today for our Baptism, forgive one person once more, and pray before the Holy Qurbono: Lord, increase our faith. Amen.
kids: Children, a mustard seed is tiny, smaller than a grain of rice. Jesus said that if our faith is even that small, it can pull up a big tree! When is it hard for you to forgive your brother, sister or friend? Ask Jesus: “Lord, give me more faith so that I can forgive.” Then go and make peace.

homily: Dear friends, Christ is risen! The Letter to the Hebrews pictures a great stadium. We are on the track, and the stands are full: since we are surrounded by so great a cloud of witnesses, let us also lay aside every weight and the sin that clings so closely, and let us run with perseverance the race that is set before us (Hebrews 12:1).

Where do we look while we run? Looking to Jesus the pioneer and perfecter of our faith, who for the sake of the joy that was set before him endured the cross (Hebrews 12:2). He has already finished the course; on Easter morning he broke through the tape of death. Consider him, says Hebrews, so that you may not grow weary or lose heart (Hebrews 12:3).

In the Gospel Jesus tells a parable about our need to pray always and not to lose heart (Luke 18:1). A poor widow keeps coming to a judge who fears neither God nor people, until he gives her justice just to be rid of her. If even he gives in, will not God grant justice to his chosen ones who cry to him day and night? (Luke 18:7). Our God is not that judge. He is our Father.

Jesus ends with a question: when the Son of Man comes, will he find faith on earth? (Luke 18:8). Let us answer it with our lives. Take up again the prayer you dropped. Keep the evening prayer at home. Come to the Holy Qurbono for strength, and run with the saints. Amen.
kids: Children, Christ is risen! Have you ever run in a race at school sports day? When you are tired, the people cheering help you keep going. The Bible says the saints in heaven are like a big crowd cheering for us. And Jesus is at the finish line! Jesus also told a story about a lady who kept asking and asking until she got help. He wants us to keep praying and never give up. What will you keep praying for this week?

homily: Dear friends, Christ is risen! Today our Church honours Mar Geevarghese Sahada, St George, a Christian soldier who gave his life for Christ in the great persecution of the early fourth century. Sahada means martyr, and martyr means witness. His tomb at Lydda drew pilgrims from very early times, and his name lives in countless Kerala families.

St Paul writes: share in suffering like a good soldier of Christ Jesus. No one serving in the army gets entangled in everyday affairs; the soldier's aim is to please the enlisting officer (2 Timothy 2:3–4). George served an earthly emperor, but his first loyalty was to Christ, who enlisted him in Baptism.

Jesus did not hide the cost: see, I am sending you out like sheep into the midst of wolves (Matthew 10:16). His witnesses would be dragged before governors and kings. But he promised: it is not you who speak, but the Spirit of your Father speaking through you, and the one who endures to the end will be saved (Matthew 10:20, 22).

The martyrs belong to Qyomtho, because no one dies for a lie: they died for the risen Lord whom they knew. The dragon of the legend is evil itself. Each time we refuse evil for Christ, we strike it. Let us pray for persecuted Christians today, and ask Mar Geevarghese for the courage to be faithful soldiers in small things. Amen.
kids: Children, Christ is risen! Today is the feast of Mar Geevarghese, St George. Do you know anyone called Varghese or George? They are named after him! He was a soldier who loved Jesus so much that he would not stop being a Christian, even when the emperor ordered him. There is a famous story of him fighting a dragon. The dragon means everything bad. When you say no to lying or hitting or cheating because you love Jesus, you are as brave as St George!

homily: Dear friends, Christ is risen! Two men went up to the temple to pray. The Pharisee prayed: God, I thank you that I am not like other people (Luke 18:11), and he gave God a list of his fasts and his gifts. The tax collector stood far off, beat his breast and said: God, be merciful to me, a sinner! (Luke 18:13).

Jesus says the second man went home justified, for all who exalt themselves will be humbled, but all who humble themselves will be exalted (Luke 18:14). The Pharisee showed God only his healthy side. The tax collector showed God his wounds, and God healed him.

Hebrews tells us how God heals: by the discipline of a Father. The Lord disciplines those whom he loves (Hebrews 12:6), for our good, in order that we may share his holiness (Hebrews 12:10). So pursue peace with everyone, and the holiness without which no one will see the Lord (Hebrews 12:14), and let no root of bitterness spring up.

In every Qurbono we pray the tax collector's prayer: Kurielaison, Lord, have mercy. Let us mean it. Today, prepare for Sunday: make a good confession if you can, and take one step to make peace with someone. The risen Lord, who was not ashamed to show his wounds, is not ashamed of ours. Amen.
kids: Children, Christ is risen! Jesus told a story about two men praying. One said: God, I am so good, better than everyone! The other said: God, I have done wrong things, please forgive me. Which one do you think made God happy? The second one! God loves it when we are honest and say sorry. In church we say Kurielaison, which means Lord, have mercy. Tonight, before you sleep, tell Jesus sorry for one thing, and he will give you a big hug of forgiveness.

homily: Dear friends, Christ is risen! Yesterday we honoured St Mark, and today we hear his Gospel. Jesus sits in a boat and teaches the crowd on the shore. His first word is: Listen! A sower went out to sow (Mark 4:3).

The seed falls on the path, on rocky ground, among thorns, and on good soil. Only the good soil yields grain, thirty and sixty and a hundredfold (Mark 4:8). The sower throws seed everywhere. God gives his word to every heart. The question is not the seed, which is always good, but the soil.

Hebrews tells us where the word is sown most solemnly. We have not come to the fire and fear of Sinai. You have come to Mount Zion and to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, and to innumerable angels in festal gathering (Hebrews 12:22), and to Jesus, whose sprinkled blood speaks a better word than the blood of Abel (Hebrews 12:24). That is the Holy Qurbono: heaven and earth singing together.

So let us prepare the soil. Read the Gospel before Sunday. Come early and be still. Keep one word from the readings all week. Pull out one thorn of worry by giving it to God in prayer. And the Lord promises a harvest. Let anyone with ears to hear listen! (Mark 4:9). Amen.
kids: Children, Christ is risen! Have you ever planted a seed? Jesus told a story about a farmer who threw seeds everywhere. Birds ate some; some dried up on the rocks; some were choked by thorns. But the seeds on good soil grew big and tall! God's words are like seeds, and your heart is like the soil. When you listen in church and remember what you heard, your heart becomes good soil. This week, try to remember one thing Jesus said, and tell it to someone at home.

homily: Dear friends, Christ is risen! Hebrews tells us that God will shake not only the earth but also the heaven, so that what cannot be shaken may remain (Hebrews 12:26–27). Many of us remember the floods of 2018. We learned then how quickly things can be swept away.

But there is something that will never be swept away: since we are receiving a kingdom that cannot be shaken, let us give thanks, by which we offer to God an acceptable worship with reverence and awe (Hebrews 12:28). That thanksgiving is the Holy Qurbono.

The rich ruler asked Jesus about eternal life, but when Jesus said, sell all that you own and distribute the money to the poor... then come, follow me, he became sad; for he was very rich (Luke 18:22–23). Peter said, look, we have left our homes and followed you, and Jesus promised: no one who has left house or family for the kingdom of God will fail to get back very much more in this age, and in the age to come eternal life (Luke 18:28–30).

Today we remember St Cletus, one of the first Bishops of Rome after St Peter, who handed on faithfully what he had received. He built on the rock. Let us pray for the Pope and our bishops, let go of one thing that holds us back, and give thanks at the altar for the kingdom that cannot be shaken. Amen.
kids: Children, Christ is risen! Have you ever built a sandcastle, and then a wave came and washed it away? Many things in this world are like that sandcastle. But Jesus gives us something that no wave can wash away: God's kingdom and his love. A rich man was sad because he did not want to share his things. But Peter left everything to follow Jesus, and Jesus gave him much more. This week, can you share one toy or book with someone who needs it?

homily: Dear friends, Christ is risen! Today our Church remembers Most Rev. Isaac Mar Yoohanon, a bishop who entered his rest in 1987. Hebrews tells us: remember your leaders, those who spoke the word of God to you; consider the outcome of their way of life, and imitate their faith. Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever (Hebrews 13:7–8).

Hebrews also says: we have an altar (Hebrews 13:10). Jesus suffered outside the city gate in order to sanctify the people by his own blood (Hebrews 13:12), and that sacrifice is made present at every Holy Qurbono. From the altar flow two more sacrifices: praise on our lips, and doing good and sharing what we have, for such sacrifices are pleasing to God (Hebrews 13:15–16).

In the Gospel Jesus asks: who then is the faithful and wise slave, whom his master has put in charge of his household, to give the other slaves their allowance of food at the proper time? (Matthew 24:45). That is the work of a bishop and a priest, but each of us is a steward too: of children, of workers, of the sick, of the poor at our gate.

Let us pray today for the soul of Mar Yoohanon and all our departed shepherds, and for our bishops now. And let us be found at work when the Lord comes: faithful at the altar, generous with our neighbours, giving food at the proper time to those who depend on us. Amen.
kids: Children, Christ is risen! Today we remember a bishop called Isaac Mar Yoohanon, who went home to God forty years ago. Bishops are like shepherds who take care of God's family. Jesus told a story about a servant who was put in charge of giving food to everyone in the house, and he did it well every day. God gives you jobs too: helping Amma, sharing with your little brother or sister, saying your prayers. If you do them well, Jesus will be very happy when he sees you!

homily: Dear friends, Christ is risen! Jesus tells of ten bridesmaids waiting with lamps for the bridegroom. Five of them were foolish, and five were wise. The wise took flasks of oil with their lamps (Matthew 25:2–4). At midnight the cry goes up: look! Here is the bridegroom! Come out to meet him (Matthew 25:6).

Those who were ready went in to the wedding banquet, and the door was shut (Matthew 25:10). The oil cannot be borrowed at the last moment. St Augustine said it is the oil of love. Keep awake therefore, for you know neither the day nor the hour (Matthew 25:13).

Paul prays: may the God of peace himself sanctify you entirely; and may your spirit and soul and body be kept sound and blameless at the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ. And he encourages us: the one who calls you is faithful, and he will do this (1 Thessalonians 5:23–24). God gives the oil, if we keep coming to him.

St Catherine of Siena, whom we remember today, was a wise virgin. A dyer's daughter with little schooling, she prayed so deeply that she became a Doctor of the Church, and she loved the Church so much that she persuaded the Pope to return to Rome. Let us ask her prayers, fill our lamps in prayer and at the Qurbono, and be ready for the Bridegroom. Amen.
kids: Children, Christ is risen! Jesus told a story about ten girls waiting for a wedding with their lamps. Five brought extra oil and five forgot. When the bridegroom came at midnight, only the girls with oil could go to the party! Jesus wants our hearts to be like lamps full of oil, ready for him. We fill them when we pray and love others. Today we remember St Catherine, a girl from Italy who prayed every day and loved Jesus with all her heart. Ask her to help you pray too!

homily: Dear friends, Christ is risen! Today our Church honours Mar Yaqob Shleeha, St James the son of Zebedee, brother of John, one of the three closest disciples of Jesus. He saw the Transfiguration and was near the Lord in Gethsemane. And Acts tells us that King Herod had James, the brother of John, killed with the sword (Acts 12:2): he was the first of the Twelve to give his life.

But in today's Gospel James has not yet understood. He and John ask: grant us to sit, one at your right hand and one at your left, in your glory. Jesus answers: you do not know what you are asking. Are you able to drink the cup that I drink? (Mark 10:37–38). They want thrones; he offers them his cup.

Then Jesus teaches all of us: whoever wishes to become great among you must be your servant... For the Son of Man came not to be served but to serve, and to give his life a ransom for many (Mark 10:43–45). James learned. An ancient account says he forgave the man who accused him with the words: peace be with you.

St Paul shows us how to live this: restore the fallen in a spirit of gentleness; bear one another's burdens; and let us not grow weary in doing what is right, for we will reap at harvest time, if we do not give up (Galatians 6:1–2, 9). Today let us serve someone who cannot repay us. That is the cup, and that is the glory. Amen.
kids: Children, Christ is risen! Today is the feast of St James, a fisherman who followed Jesus. Jesus called James and his brother John sons of thunder, because they were so loud and full of energy! Once they asked Jesus for the best seats. Jesus said: the greatest is the one who helps others. Jesus himself came to serve us. This week, be like St James after he learned: help at home without being asked, and you will be great in God's eyes!

intro: Theme: “Peace be with you: sent, forgiven, believing.”
On New Sunday the Risen Lord comes through locked doors. He gives peace, breathes the Spirit, entrusts the power to forgive sins, and leads Thomas from doubt to faith.

sub: The disciples hide in fear; Jesus comes and stands among them.
His first word is “Peace”, not reproach.
Isaiah tells the herald of good tidings: “lift up your voice … do not fear.” The Risen Christ turns fear into mission.
q: Get you up to a high mountain, O Zion, herald of good tidings; lift up your voice with strength, O Jerusalem, herald of good tidings, lift it up, do not fear.

When it was evening on that day, the first day of the week, and the doors of the house where the disciples had met were locked for fear of the Jews, Jesus came and stood among them and said, “Peace be with you.”
points.apply: Bring your fears to the Risen Lord in prayer; let him say to you: “Peace be with you.”

points.h: Sent with the Spirit to forgive
sub: Elisha asked for a double share of Elijah's spirit to continue his mission.
Jesus breathes on the apostles: “Receive the Holy Spirit.”
He gives them power to forgive sins: the gift of the sacrament of Reconciliation.
q: Elisha said, “Please let me inherit a double share of your spirit.”

Jesus said to them again, “Peace be with you. As the Father has sent me, so I send you.” When he had said this, he breathed on them and said to them, “Receive the Holy Spirit. If you forgive the sins of any, they are forgiven them.”
points.apply: Make an Easter confession if you have not yet done so.

points.h: Blessed are those who have not seen
sub: The Lord does not abandon doubting Thomas; like a shepherd he comes back for the one.
He shows his wounds; Thomas confesses: “My Lord and my God!”
We are among those blessed who believe without seeing.
q: He will feed his flock like a shepherd; he will gather the lambs in his arms, and carry them in his bosom, and gently lead the mother sheep.
Then he said to Thomas, “Put your finger here and see my hands. Reach out your hand and put it in my side. Do not doubt but believe.” Thomas answered him, “My Lord and my God!”
points.apply: At the elevation in the Qurbono, say silently: “My Lord and my God.”

concl: Peace, Spirit, mercy and faith: these are the gifts of the Risen Lord on New Sunday.
Let us receive them and become messengers of his peace.
2027-04-04.resolve: Forgive one person this week, as Christ forgives you.

intro: Theme: “It is the Lord!”

After the Resurrection the disciples go back to fishing on the lake. All night they catch nothing. At dawn a stranger tells them where to cast the net, and they recognise him. He has prepared breakfast for them.

sub: Peter says “I am going fishing”: back to the old life.
“That night they caught nothing”: our efforts without the Lord bear little fruit.
The Psalmist knew it: unless the Lord builds the house, the builders labour in vain.
q: Unless the LORD builds the house, those who build it labor in vain.
Simon Peter said to them, “I am going fishing.” They said to him, “We will go with you.” They went out and got into the boat, but that night they caught nothing.
points.apply: Begin each workday this week with a short prayer offering your work to God.

sub: At dawn Jesus stands on the shore; they do not recognise him.
They obey: “Cast the net to the right side”, and the net is full.
The beloved disciple sees with the eyes of love: “It is the Lord!”
q: The LORD is my strength and my might, and he has become my salvation; this is my God, and I will praise him.

He said to them, “Cast the net to the right side of the boat, and you will find some.” So they cast it, and now they were not able to haul it in because there were so many fish. That disciple whom Jesus loved said to Peter, “It is the Lord!”
points.apply: Where have you failed recently? Try again, this time at his word and with prayer.

sub: The Risen Lord has lit a fire and prepared bread and fish.
He takes the bread and gives it to them: the gesture of the Eucharist.
“Taste and see that the Lord is good”: in the Qurbono he still feeds tired disciples.
q: O taste and see that the LORD is good; happy are those who take refuge in him.
Jesus said to them, “Come and have breakfast.” … Jesus came and took the bread and gave it to them, and did the same with the fish.
points.apply: Come to Holy Qurbono this week not as a duty but as an invitation from a friend.

concl: The Risen Lord meets us in our ordinary work and our empty nights.
Let us obey his word, recognise him with love, and come to his table.
2027-04-11.resolve: Share a meal this week with someone who is lonely.

intro: Theme: “Stay with us, Lord.”

Two disappointed disciples walk away from Jerusalem. The Risen Lord walks with them unrecognised, opens the Scriptures, and is known in the breaking of the bread. Emmaus is the shape of every Holy Qurbono: Word, Bread, Mission.

points.h: He walks with us in disappointment
sub: “We had hoped …”: they walk away sad, their hopes buried.
Jesus comes near and walks with them, though they do not recognise him.
God seeks even those who are not seeking him.
q: I was ready to be sought out by those who did not ask, to be found by those who did not seek me. I said, “Here I am, here I am.”
While they were talking and discussing, Jesus himself came near and went with them, but their eyes were kept from recognizing him.
points.apply: Tell the Lord honestly about your disappointments; he is walking with you.

sub: Beginning with Moses and all the prophets, Jesus explains the Scriptures about himself.
Their hearts burn within them: the Word prepares for recognition.
In the Qurbono the readings and homily are this road to Emmaus.
q: Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path.
They said to each other, “Were not our hearts burning within us while he was talking to us on the road, while he was opening the scriptures to us?”
points.apply: Read the Sunday Gospel at home before you come to church.

points.h: Known in the breaking of the bread
sub: “Stay with us, because it is almost evening”: they invite him in.
He takes bread, blesses, breaks and gives: their eyes are opened.
At once they return to Jerusalem to tell the others: every Qurbono ends in mission.
q: Come, eat of my bread and drink of the wine I have mixed.
When he was at the table with them, he took bread, blessed and broke it, and gave it to them. Then their eyes were opened, and they recognized him.
points.apply: After Qurbono, share the joy of faith with one person at home or at work.

concl: The Lord walks with us, speaks to us and feeds us.
Let us say each day: “Stay with us, Lord,” and run to tell others that he is risen.
2027-04-18.resolve: Pray each evening this week: “Stay with us, Lord, for it is evening.”

intro: Theme: “I am with you always.”
The Risen Lord shows the disciples his hands and feet, opens their minds to the Scriptures, and sends them to all nations. The Gospel of this Sunday is the Church's charter of mission.

points.h: “Look at my hands”: a real, risen Lord
sub: The disciples are frightened and think they see a ghost.
Jesus shows his wounds: the Risen One is the Crucified One, truly alive in his body.
God never forgets us: our names are inscribed on the palms of his hands.
q: Can a woman forget her nursing child, or show no compassion for the child of her womb? Even these may forget, yet I will not forget you. See, I have inscribed you on the palms of my hands.
He said to them, “Why are you frightened, and why do doubts arise in your hearts? Look at my hands and my feet; see that it is I myself.”
points.apply: In moments of fear this week, look at a crucifix and remember: he has not forgotten you.

sub: God revealed himself to Moses as merciful and gracious.
Repentance and forgiveness are to be proclaimed in Christ's name to all nations.
Peter learns that God shows no partiality: every nation is welcome.
q: The LORD, the LORD, a God merciful and gracious, slow to anger, and abounding in steadfast love and faithfulness.
Then Peter began to speak to them: “I truly understand that God shows no partiality, but in every nation anyone who fears him and does what is right is acceptable to him.”
points.apply: Reject every prejudice against people of other castes, languages or religions.

sub: God made his Servant a covenant for the people.
All authority is given to Jesus; he sends us to baptise and teach.
He does not send us alone: “I am with you always, to the end of the age.”
q: In a time of favor I have answered you, on a day of salvation I have helped you; I have kept you and given you as a covenant to the people.

Go therefore and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, and teaching them to obey everything that I have commanded you. And remember, I am with you always, to the end of the age.
points.apply: Support the missions with prayer and an offering; teach the faith to the children in your family.

concl: The Risen Christ shows his wounds, opens the Scriptures, forgives and sends.
Let us be his witnesses, confident that he is with us always.
2027-04-25.resolve: Pray for missionaries, especially those from Kerala serving in other lands.

intro: Theme: “He is God not of the dead, but of the living.”
On Thursday of Hevoro week: a question built as a trap, the God of Abraham who is the God of the living, and Jesus crowned with glory.

points.h: The question built as a trap
sub: Seven brothers and one wife.
Not knowing the Scriptures.
Not knowing the power of God.
q: Your dead shall live, their corpses shall rise. O dwellers in the dust, awake and sing for joy!
I am the resurrection and the life. Those who believe in me, even though they die, will live
points.apply: When someone mocks the faith, answer with patience, from the Scriptures, and with trust in God's power.

sub: The burning bush.
“I am,” not “I was.”
Our departed are alive to God.
q: I am the God of your father, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.
If we live, we live to the Lord, and if we die, we die to the Lord; so then, whether we live or whether we die, we are the Lord’s.
points.apply: Pray for your departed by name this week at the Holy Qurbono, with Easter hope.

sub: Psalm 8 and human dignity.
Not yet everything in subjection.
Crowned because he tasted death for everyone.
q: what are human beings that you are mindful of them, mortals that you care for them?
Therefore God also highly exalted him and gave him the name that is above every name,
points.apply: When life is unfinished or unfair, fix your eyes on the risen Jesus, already crowned.

concl: God is the God of the living, and in the risen Jesus human nature is already crowned with glory.
Our departed are alive to God, and the Holy Qurbono is the pledge of our own rising.
2027-04-01.resolve: Live this Hevoro week as people of the resurrection: praying for the departed with hope, honoring marriage as a road to heaven, and answering doubt with patience.

intro: Theme: “Everyone therefore who acknowledges me before others, I also will acknowledge before my Father in heaven.”
On the Friday of All the Confessors: the witnesses of whom the world was not worthy, the Lord's word against fear, and his promise to all who confess him.

points.h: Of whom the world was not worthy
sub: The named and the unnamed heroes of faith.
Chains, exile, the sword.
Robes made white in the blood of the Lamb.
q: If our God whom we serve is able to deliver us from the furnace of blazing fire and out of your hand, O king, let him deliver us.
These are they who have come out of the great ordeal; they have washed their robes and made them white in the blood of the Lamb.
points.apply: Pray today by name for Christians who suffer for the faith, and help them if you can.

sub: Nothing hidden stays hidden.
They cannot kill the soul.
Two sparrows and the hairs of your head.
q: Do not fear, for I have redeemed you; I have called you by name, you are mine.
There is no fear in love, but perfect love casts out fear;
points.apply: Name one fear that keeps you silent about Christ, and hand it over to him in prayer.

sub: Confession with the lips.
Small confessions in daily life.
The Lord acknowledges his own before the Father.
q: Precious in the sight of the LORD is the death of his faithful ones.
because if you confess with your lips that Jesus is Lord and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved.
points.apply: Make one small, gentle confession of Christ today in a place where it costs you something.

concl: The confessors share the Lord's death and now his victory; in the white week we see them robed in white.
The risen Lord who counts the hairs of our head will acknowledge before his Father all who acknowledge him.
2027-04-02.resolve: Confess Christ gently and without fear: pray for the persecuted, ask the Virgin Mary, Queen of Confessors, for courage, and receive strength at the Holy Qurbono.

intro: Theme: “We are his house if we hold firm the confidence and the pride that belong to hope.”
On Saturday of Hevoro week: Jesus the apostle and high priest, the house of God that we are, and the generosity that rejoices in all good done in his name.

sub: The apostle sent to us.
The high priest who goes for us to the Father.
Both completed in his Death and Resurrection.
q: Not so with my servant Moses; he is entrusted with all my house.
Since, then, we have a great high priest who has passed through the heavens, Jesus, the Son of God, let us hold fast to our confession.
points.apply: Spend five quiet minutes today simply looking at Jesus, in a crucifix or an icon of the Resurrection.

sub: Moses the faithful servant.
Christ the Son and builder.
Living stones held together by hope.
q: Unless the LORD builds the house, those who build it labor in vain.
like living stones, let yourselves be built into a spiritual house, to be a holy priesthood, to offer spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ.
points.apply: Do one thing this week that builds up your parish: a visit, a job done, a word of encouragement.

sub: John's jealousy.
Moses and the prophets outside the camp.
Rejoicing in every good done in Jesus' name.
q: Would that all the LORD’s people were prophets, and that the LORD would put his spirit on them!
What does it matter? Just this, that Christ is proclaimed in every way, whether out of false motives or true; and in that I rejoice.
points.apply: Thank God aloud for one good work done by people outside your own circle, and help it if you can.

concl: Jesus is the apostle and high priest of our confession, the faithful Son over God's house.
We are his house, built together by hope and generous enough to rejoice in all good done in his name.
2027-04-03.resolve: Close the white week by holding firm your hope, going to confession if you can, and coming to New Sunday ready to confess with Thomas, My Lord and my God.

intro: Theme: “Remember Jesus Christ, raised from the dead, a descendant of David.”
On Monday after New Sunday: the word that no chain can bind, the faithfulness that outlasts our failures, and the rejected stone that became the cornerstone.

points.h: The word of God is not chained
sub: Paul writes from prison.
To remember is to let God act now.
Ignatius of Antioch writes on the road to Rome.
q: so shall my word be that goes out from my mouth; it shall not return to me empty,
proclaiming the kingdom of God and teaching about the Lord Jesus Christ with all boldness and without hindrance.
points.apply: Say on waking and before sleep: “Remember Jesus Christ, raised from the dead.”

sub: If we have died with him, we will live with him.
If we endure, we will reign with him.
Even when we are faithless.
q: The steadfast love of the LORD never ceases, his mercies never come to an end; they are new every morning; great is your faithfulness.
God is faithful; by him you were called into the fellowship of his Son, Jesus Christ our Lord.
points.apply: If you have drifted since Easter, return to the Lord in confession this week.

points.h: The stone that the builders rejected
sub: The vineyard and its tenants.
The beloved son.
Raised up as the cornerstone.
q: The stone that the builders rejected has become the chief cornerstone.
There is salvation in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven given among mortals by which we must be saved.
points.apply: Give the Lord his share this week: a part of your time, money or gifts, offered consciously to him.

concl: The word of God is not chained, and the risen Christ remains faithful even when we are not.
The Son who was rejected is the cornerstone on which God builds his Church.
2027-04-05.resolve: Remember Jesus Christ, raised from the dead, every morning and night; give God the fruit of the vineyard he has entrusted to you; pray for all who are in chains.

intro: Theme: “But God, who is rich in mercy… made us alive together with Christ.”
On Tuesday after New Sunday: the mercy that raised us with Christ, the Lord who rebukes the fever and raises up for service, and the good works prepared for us.

sub: Dead through trespasses.
Made alive, raised up, seated with Christ.
By grace, not by our own doing.
q: Thus says the Lord GOD to these bones: I will cause breath to enter you, and you shall live.
And when you were dead in trespasses and the uncircumcision of your flesh, God made you alive together with him, when he forgave us all our trespasses,
points.apply: Find the date of your Baptism and thank God for it this evening.

sub: The Lord enters Simon's house.
He rebukes the fever.
At sunset he lays hands on each one.
q: Surely he has borne our infirmities and carried our diseases;
For the Son of Man came not to be served but to serve, and to give his life a ransom for many.
points.apply: Bring one sick person to the Lord in prayer at the Holy Qurbono this week, and visit or call them.

sub: God's workmanship.
Grace that is never idle.
Works prepared beforehand to be our way of life.
q: He has told you, O mortal, what is good; and what does the LORD require of you but to do justice, and to love kindness, and to walk humbly with your God?
In the same way, let your light shine before others, so that they may see your good works and give glory to your Father in heaven.
points.apply: Do one service today at once, without being asked and without waiting to feel like it.

concl: Easter has begun in us through Baptism: God, rich in mercy, made us alive with Christ.
The Lord who heals us raises us up to serve, in the good works he has prepared.
2027-04-06.resolve: Thank God for your Baptism, ask him to rebuke the fever in you, and rise at once to serve.

intro: Theme: “For he is our peace.”
On Wednesday after New Sunday: those far off brought near, the wall broken down in Christ's flesh, and the listening heart that lets the light shine.

points.h: Brought near by the blood of Christ
sub: Once far off, without hope.
The commonwealth of Israel and the covenants of promise.
Grafted into Israel's hope.
q: Peace, peace, to the far and the near, says the LORD; and I will heal them.
There is no longer Jew or Greek, there is no longer slave or free, there is no longer male and female; for all of you are one in Christ Jesus.
points.apply: Thank God today for the gift of faith that brought you near, and pray for the Jewish people.

sub: The wall broken down in his flesh.
Hostility put to death on the Cross.
Access in one Spirit to the Father.
q: For a child has been born for us, a son given to us; authority rests upon his shoulders; and he is named Wonderful Counselor, Mighty God, Everlasting Father, Prince of Peace.
Peace I leave with you; my peace I give to you. I do not give to you as the world gives.
points.apply: Take one step this week toward someone you have kept at a distance.

points.h: Pay attention to how you listen
sub: The lamp on the lampstand.
To those who have, more will be given.
The Teacher within.
q: Speak, for your servant is listening.
But be doers of the word, and not merely hearers who deceive themselves.
points.apply: Before the readings at the Holy Qurbono, pray to hear them as if for the first time.

concl: The risen Christ is our peace: he has broken down every dividing wall and brought all into one Body.
His light is not for hiding, and those who listen with faith receive more.
2027-04-07.resolve: Stop rebuilding the walls Christ has broken: take one step toward reconciliation, pray for Christian unity, and listen to God's word with a ready heart.

intro: Theme: “Remember your leaders, those who spoke the word of God to you; consider the outcome of their way of life, and imitate their faith.”
On the memory of Most Rev. Lawrence Mar Ephrem: remembering our shepherds, the faithful steward, and the altar from which we live.

sub: Remember those who spoke God's word.
Consider how their lives ended.
Imitate their faith.
q: Remember the days of old, consider the years long past; ask your father, and he will inform you; your elders, and they will tell you.
I have fought the good fight, I have finished the race, I have kept the faith.
points.apply: Pray today by name for a bishop, priest or teacher who brought you the faith.

points.h: The same yesterday, today and forever
sub: Shepherds pass; the Chief Shepherd does not.
The risen Lord has not changed.
Do not be carried away by strange teachings.
q: For I the Lord do not change; therefore you, O children of Jacob, have not perished.
Jesus said to them, “Very truly, I tell you, before Abraham was, I am.”
points.apply: Hold fast this week to one truth of the Creed you are tempted to doubt, and thank God for it.

points.h: The faithful steward at the altar
sub: Food for the household at the proper time.
We have an altar.
The sacrifice of praise and of sharing.
q: I will offer to you a thanksgiving sacrifice and call on the name of the Lord.
Moreover, it is required of stewards that they be found trustworthy.
points.apply: Share one thing you have this week with someone in need, as a sacrifice pleasing to God.

concl: Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever; the shepherds who served us handed on the one risen Lord.
We eat from his altar and go out to offer praise and to share what we have.
2027-04-08.resolve: Remember your shepherds in prayer, be a faithful steward of what the Lord has given you, and let him find you at work when he comes.

intro: Theme: “The one who formerly was persecuting us is now proclaiming the faith he once tried to destroy. And they glorified God because of me.”
On Friday after New Sunday: the grace that called Paul, the hidden years, and the child at the Lord's side.

sub: Set apart before birth.
God was pleased to reveal his Son.
Zeal turned, not destroyed.
q: Before I formed you in the womb I knew you, and before you were born I consecrated you; I appointed you a prophet to the nations.
But by the grace of God I am what I am, and his grace toward me has not been in vain.
points.apply: Thank God tonight for one way his grace has turned your life.

sub: Not first to the front.
Arabia and Damascus.
Fifteen days with Cephas.
q: Therefore, I will now allure her, and bring her into the wilderness, and speak tenderly to her.
In the morning, while it was still very dark, he got up and went out to a deserted place, and there he prayed.
points.apply: Give God fifteen quiet minutes each day this week, before your phone and before your work.

sub: An argument about greatness.
A child by his side.
Welcome the least in his name.
q: But I have calmed and quieted my soul, like a weaned child with its mother; my soul is like the weaned child that is with me.
Whoever becomes humble like this child is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven.
points.apply: Step back from one argument this week about who is right or who is first.

concl: The risen Lord turned the persecutor into the apostle, and his grace can turn anyone.
A changed and humble life makes others glorify God.
2027-04-09.resolve: Pray for one you have given up on, give God hidden time each day, and welcome the least in the name of Jesus.

intro: Theme: “Whoever listens to you listens to me, and whoever rejects you rejects me, and whoever rejects me rejects the one who sent me.”
On Saturday after New Sunday: running with the apostles, the freedom of the Gospel, and the danger of hearing without changing.

points.h: The freedom we have in Christ
sub: Titus was not compelled.
Saved by grace, not by achievement.
Freedom to live by the Spirit.
q: The spirit of the Lord God is upon me, because the Lord has anointed me; he has sent me to bring good news to the oppressed, to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and release to the prisoners;
For freedom Christ has set us free. Stand firm, therefore, and do not submit again to a yoke of slavery.
points.apply: Name one fear or habit that still enslaves you, and bring it to confession this Easter season.

sub: Fourteen years, and still he asked.
The gospel laid before the apostles.
One faith in one communion.
q: How very good and pleasant it is when kindred live together in unity!
It is by your holding fast to the word of life that I can boast on the day of Christ that I did not run in vain or labor in vain.
points.apply: Before you share a strong opinion about the faith, check it this week with the Catechism or a priest.

sub: Chorazin saw and did not repent.
Christ speaks through his messengers.
Like Mary, hear and keep the word.
q: And the people of Nineveh believed God; they proclaimed a fast, and everyone, great and small, put on sackcloth.
But be doers of the word, and not merely hearers who deceive themselves.
points.apply: Choose one word from tomorrow's Gospel and do it before next Saturday.

concl: Paul ran in communion with the apostles and defended the freedom we have in Christ.
Christ speaks through his Church; to listen is to be changed.
2027-04-10.resolve: Come to the Holy Qurbono tomorrow ready to listen, and let one word of the risen Lord change your week.

intro: Theme: “Whoever welcomes you welcomes me, and whoever welcomes me welcomes the one who sent me.”
On the commemoration of St Julius, Pope: the peace of Easter, the hope that suffering produces, and the welcome that receives Christ.

sub: Justified by faith.
Access to the grace in which we stand.
Raised for our justification.
q: the Lord lift up his countenance upon you, and give you peace.
Peace I leave with you; my peace I give to you. I do not give to you as the world gives. Do not let your hearts be troubled, and do not let them be afraid.
points.apply: Make your peace with God this Easter season in the sacrament of Reconciliation, and with one person you have hurt.

sub: Endurance.
Character.
A hope that does not disappoint.
q: But he knows the way that I take; when he has tested me, I shall come out like gold.
My brothers and sisters, whenever you face trials of any kind, consider it nothing but joy, because you know that the testing of your faith produces endurance;
points.apply: Offer one difficulty this week to the risen Lord, and ask him for endurance and hope.

sub: St Julius welcomed St Athanasius.
He guarded the faith of Nicaea.
A cup of cold water.
q: Is it not to share your bread with the hungry, and bring the homeless poor into your house; when you see the naked, to cover them, and not to hide yourself from your own kin?
Do not neglect to show hospitality to strangers, for by doing that some have entertained angels without knowing it.
points.apply: Give one cup of cold water this week: a meal, a visit or a word of welcome to someone far from home.

concl: The risen Lord has given us peace with God, and in him even suffering becomes hope.
St Julius welcomed the persecuted shepherd and so welcomed Christ.
2027-04-12.resolve: Stand firm in the faith we confess in the Creed, and welcome the least in the name of Jesus.

intro: Theme: “In the days of his flesh, Jesus offered up prayers and supplications, with loud cries and tears, to the one who was able to save him from death, and he was heard because of his reverent submission.”
On Tuesday after the Second Sunday after Qyomtho: the tears of the Son, the priest forever, and the prayer he taught us.

sub: The night of Gethsemane.
He was heard.
The Father's answer was the Resurrection.
q: I love the Lord, because he has heard my voice and my supplications.
He said, “Abba, Father, for you all things are possible; remove this cup from me; yet, not what I want, but what you want.”
points.apply: Bring one sorrow to God in prayer this week, honestly, with the words of Jesus: not what I want, but what you want.

sub: He did not glorify himself.
After the order of Melchizedek.
He lives to intercede for us.
q: The Lord has sworn and will not change his mind, “You are a priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek.”
Consequently he is able for all time to save those who approach God through him, since he always lives to make intercession for them.
points.apply: At your next Holy Qurbono, unite your own needs with the offering of Christ the High Priest.

sub: The disciples watched him pray.
Father, hallowed be your name.
Forgive as we forgive.
q: Let my prayer be counted as incense before you, and the lifting up of my hands as an evening sacrifice.
For you did not receive a spirit of slavery to fall back into fear, but you have received a spirit of adoption. When we cry, “Abba! Father!”
points.apply: Pray the Our Father slowly once each day this week, and forgive one person by name.

concl: The Son prayed with tears and was heard; the Father answered with the Resurrection.
Our High Priest forever teaches us to call God Father.
2027-04-13.resolve: Pray as sons and daughters, bring your tears to the Father, and forgive as you have been forgiven.

intro: Theme: “Ask, and it will be given you; search, and you will find; knock, and the door will be opened for you.”
On the commemoration of Mar Shemun Bar Sabbae: growing toward perfection, the ground that bears fruit, and the prayer that receives the Holy Spirit.

sub: The foundation is laid.
Now the Lord builds.
Do not settle down after Easter.
q: but those who wait for the Lord shall renew their strength, they shall mount up with wings like eagles, they shall run and not be weary, they shall walk and not faint.

Beloved, I do not consider that I have made it my own; but this one thing I do: forgetting what lies behind and straining forward to what lies ahead, I press on toward the goal for the prize of the heavenly call of God in Christ Jesus.
points.apply: Choose one step of growth this Easter season: daily Scripture, a weekday Holy Qurbono, or a work of mercy.

points.h: The ground that drinks the rain
sub: Easter is rain.
A crop useful to others.
Mar Shemun and the one who came back.
q: For as the rain and the snow come down from heaven, and do not return there until they have watered the earth, making it bring forth and sprout, giving seed to the sower and bread to the eater,
My Father is glorified by this, that you bear much fruit and become my disciples.
points.apply: Pray this week for one person who has fallen away, and for Christians persecuted today.

sub: The friend at midnight.
Persistence in prayer.
The Father gives the Holy Spirit.
q: I will put my spirit within you, and make you follow my statutes and be careful to observe my ordinances.
Likewise the Spirit helps us in our weakness; for we do not know how to pray as we ought, but that very Spirit intercedes with sighs too deep for words.
points.apply: Pray every day until Pentecost: “Heavenly Father, give me your Holy Spirit.”

concl: The risen Lord has watered us with grace; he wants a harvest, not a pause.
Mar Shemun's courage came from the God he would not deny; the Father gives the Spirit to those who ask.
2027-04-14.resolve: Grow, bear fruit, and keep knocking: ask the Father every day for the Holy Spirit as we walk toward Pentecost.

intro: Theme: “Through the power of an indestructible life.”
On this Easter weekday: the priest who cannot die, the narrow door, and the banquet that gathers east and west.

sub: Not the order of Aaron, but of Melchizedek.
Not physical descent, but an indestructible life.
He always lives to intercede for us.
q: And King Melchizedek of Salem brought out bread and wine; he was priest of God Most High.
Consequently he is able for all time to save those who approach God through him, since he always lives to make intercession for them.
points.apply: At the Holy Qurbono this week, entrust one person you love to the intercession of Christ the High Priest.

sub: “Will only a few be saved?”
“We ate and drank with you”: nearness is not yet entrance.
Narrow for the proud, wide for the humble.
q: This is the gate of the Lord; the righteous shall enter through it.
I am the gate. Whoever enters by me will be saved, and will come in and go out and find pasture.
points.apply: Do one humble act today that your pride has been resisting: an apology, a request for help, a confession.

sub: The table of the kingdom is wide.
We are among those who came from the east.
The last may be first.
q: For from the rising of the sun to its setting my name is great among the nations, and in every place incense is offered to my name, and a pure offering.
I tell you, many will come from east and west and will eat with Abraham and Isaac and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven.
points.apply: Invite one person who has stopped coming to church to the Holy Qurbono with you this Sunday.

concl: Our high priest is the risen Christ, who lives for ever and brings us to God.
The door is narrow because it is Christ himself; through him the way is open to all who come humbly.
2027-04-15.resolve: This week, enter by the narrow door in one concrete choice, and pray daily for priests.

intro: Theme: “You will be repaid at the resurrection of the righteous.”
On this Easter Friday: the blood of the new covenant, the lowest place, and the generosity that waits for the resurrection.

points.h: The blood of the new covenant
sub: A covenant that is also a will.
Sinai's blood and the cup of the Upper Room.
The testator rose to give the inheritance himself.
q: Moses took the blood and dashed it on the people, and said, “See the blood of the covenant that the Lord has made with you in accordance with all these words.”
For this is my blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins.
points.apply: Before receiving Holy Communion this week, thank the Lord in silence for one gift of his covenant.

sub: Guests choosing places of honour.
“Friend, move up higher.”
The way of the humbled and exalted Lord.
q: Do not put yourself forward in the king's presence or stand in the place of the great; for it is better to be told, “Come up here,” than to be put lower in the presence of a noble.
He humbled himself and became obedient to the point of death
points.apply: At your next gathering, choose the lower seat gladly and serve others first.

sub: Not only friends and rich neighbours.
The poor, the crippled, the lame, the blind.
No unreturned kindness is lost.
q: Since there will never cease to be some in need on the earth, I therefore command you, “Open your hand to the poor and needy neighbor in your land.”
Has not God chosen the poor in the world to be rich in faith and to be heirs of the kingdom that he has promised to those who love him?
points.apply: Share a meal this week with someone who cannot repay you.

concl: By his Blood Christ made us heirs, and by his Resurrection he gives us the inheritance.
Those who take the lowest place and open their tables to the poor will be repaid at the resurrection of the righteous.
2027-04-16.resolve: This week, give one gift and one place of honour to someone who can never pay you back.

intro: Theme: “Come; for everything is ready now.”
On the Saturday before the Third Sunday after the Resurrection: the one sacrifice, the new covenant written on hearts, and the great dinner.

sub: The priests stand day after day.
Christ offered once and sat down.
The Holy Qurbono makes the one sacrifice present.
q: The Lord says to my lord, “Sit at my right hand until I make your enemies your footstool.”
The death he died, he died to sin, once for all; but the life he lives, he lives to God.
points.apply: At the Holy Qurbono tomorrow, unite your week, its work and its troubles, with the one offering of Christ.

points.h: Written on hearts, remembered no more
sub: The Spirit bears witness.
God's law inside us.
Sins remembered no more.
q: But this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, says the Lord: I will put my law within them, and I will write it on their hearts; and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.
